translations.literal: Biographies 66: Virtuous Officials — Lu Kezhong, Niu Dechang, Fan Chengji, Wang Zheng, Zhang Yi, Li Zhan, Liu Minxing, Fu Shenwei, Liu Huan, Gao Changfu, Sun Deyuan, Zhao Jian, Pucha Zhengliu, Nuxilie Shouyu, Shi Moyuan, Zhang Gou, Zhao Zhongfu, Wu Dou, Geshilie De, Zhang Teli, Wang Hao
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 66: Virtuous Officials — Lu Kezhong, Niu Dechang, Fan Chengji, Wang Zheng, Zhang Yi, Li Zhan, Liu Minxing, Fu Shenwei, Liu Huan, Gao Changfu, Sun Deyuan, Zhao Jian, Pucha Zhengliu, Nuxilie Shouyu, Shi Moyuan, Zhang Gou, Zhao Zhongfu, Wu Dou, Geshilie De, Zhang Teli, and Wang Hao

sentences.zh: 金自穆宗號令諸部不得稱都孛堇，於是諸部始列於統屬。

translations.literal: From the time of the Jin Emperor Muzong, when he ordered the various tribes not to call themselves tribal chieftains (dubielie), the tribes were for the first time arrayed under unified command.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Muzong of Jin, the various tribes were forbidden to style themselves tribal chieftains, and for the first time they were brought into a single chain of command.

sentences.zh: 太祖命三百戶為謀克，十謀克為猛安，一如郡縣置吏之法。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered that three hundred households form a company (mouke), and ten companies form a battalion (meng'an), exactly like the method of appointing officials in commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor organized three hundred households into a company (mouke) and ten companies into a battalion (meng'an), mirroring the way officials were posted in the commandery-and-county system.

sentences.zh: 太宗既有中原，申畫封疆，分建守令。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizong gained the Central Plains, he delineated the borders afresh and established guard and magistrate posts throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Taizong held the Central Plains, he redrew the frontiers and set up prefectural guards and county magistrates across the realm.

sentences.zh: 熙宗遣廉察之使循行四方。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong sent integrity inspectors to tour all four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong dispatched integrity inspectors to travel through every region of the empire.

sentences.zh: 世宗承海陵凋镨之餘，休養生息，迄於明昌、承安之間，民物滋殖，循吏迭出焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong inherited the aftermath of Emperor Hailing's devastation and exhaustion; he nursed the people and allowed recovery to rest. By the reigns of Mingchang and Cheng'an, the population and goods multiplied, and virtuous officials appeared one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took over after the ruin left by Emperor Hailing and gave the realm time to heal. By the Mingchang and Cheng'an eras the people and their goods had flourished again, and virtuous officials rose in succession.

sentences.zh: 泰和用兵，郡縣多故，吏治衰矣。

translations.literal: During the Tahe period military campaigns were launched; commanderies and counties saw many disturbances, and the administration of officials declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tahe reign turned to war, commanderies and counties were beset by troubles, and official governance fell into decline.

sentences.zh: 宣宗尚刀筆之習，嚴考核之法，能吏不乏，而豈弟之政罕見稱述焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong valued the habits of the clerical brush and enforced strict assessment methods; capable officials were not lacking, but mild and benevolent governance was rarely spoken of with praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong favored the ways of the clerk's brush and tightened performance reviews; capable administrators were plentiful, yet mild, brotherly rule was seldom praised in the records.

sentences.zh: 金百餘年吏治，始終可考，於是作《循吏傳》。

translations.literal: The administration of officials across Jin's hundred-odd years may be traced from beginning to end; therefore the "Biographies of Virtuous Officials" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Jin dynasty's century and more of official governance, the record can be followed from start to finish; hence these biographies of virtuous officials were written.

sentences.zh: 盧克忠

translations.literal: Lu Kezhong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kezhong

sentences.zh: 盧克忠，貴德州奉集人。

translations.literal: Lu Kezhong was a native of Fengji in Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kezhong came from Fengji in Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高永昌據遼陽，克忠走詣金源郡王斡魯營降，遂以撒屋出為鄉導。

translations.literal: When Gao Yongchang held Liaoyang, Kezhong fled to the camp of Prince Jin Yuan, Wulu, to surrender, and then served as a local guide with Sawu as his base.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang seized Liaoyang, Kezhong made his way to Prince Jin Yuan Wulu's camp to submit, and thereafter guided the army from his home district of Sawu.

sentences.zh: 斡魯克東京，永昌走長松島，克忠與渤海人撻不也追獲之。

translations.literal: Wulu captured the Eastern Capital; Yongchang fled to Changsong Island, and Kezhong, together with the Bohai man Tabuye, pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Wulu took the Eastern Capital, and Yongchang fled to Changsong Island; Kezhong and the Bohai commander Tabuye ran him down and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 收國二年，授世襲謀克。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shouguo, he was granted a hereditary company command (mouke).
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shouguo he received a hereditary company command.

sentences.zh: 其後，定燕伐宋皆與有功，除登州刺史，改刺澶州。

translations.literal: Thereafter he took part with merit in the pacification of Yan and the campaign against Song; he was appointed prefect of Dengzhou and later transferred as military commissioner of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later distinguished himself in the pacification of Yan and the war against Song, was made prefect of Dengzhou, and then reassigned as military commissioner of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 天德間，同知保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: During the Tiande era he served as deputy military commissioner of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande reign he served as deputy commissioner of the Baoda military circuit.

sentences.zh: 綏德州軍卒數人道過鄜城，求宿民家，是夜有賊剽主人財而去。

translations.literal: Several soldiers from Suide Prefecture passed through Fucheng on the road and asked to lodge in a private home; that night thieves robbed the host's property and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A few soldiers from Suide Prefecture were traveling through Fucheng and asked to stay overnight in a civilian house; that night robbers stripped the host of his goods and fled.

sentences.zh: 有司執假宿之卒，系獄榜掠誣服。

translations.literal: The authorities seized the soldiers who had lodged there under false pretenses, imprisoned them, flogged them under torture, and obtained a false confession.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities arrested the soldiers who had lodged there, threw them in prison, beat them until they confessed to a crime they had not committed.

sentences.zh: 克忠察其冤，獨不肯署，未幾果得賊，假宿之卒遂釋。

translations.literal: Kezhong perceived their injustice and alone refused to sign the warrant; before long the real thieves were caught, and the soldiers who had lodged there were released.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhong saw that they had been wronged and alone refused to endorse the case; soon the real thieves were caught, and the soldiers who had stayed overnight were freed.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，除北京副留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was appointed deputy guardian of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was made deputy guardian of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會民艱食，克忠下令凡民有蓄積者計留一歲，悉平其價糴之，由是無捐瘠之患。

translations.literal: When the people were suffering from scarce food, Kezhong ordered that whoever among the populace had stores should be allowed to keep enough for one year and sell the rest at a fair price; thereby there was no plague of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: When famine pressed on the people, Kezhong ordered that anyone with grain reserves keep a year's supply and sell the rest at a fair price; in this way the district escaped the scourge of emaciation and death.

sentences.zh: 轉陳州防禦使，後以靜難軍節度使致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defender of Chenzhou, later retired as military commissioner of the Jingnan Army, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defender of Chenzhou, later retired as commissioner of the Jingnan circuit, and died.

sentences.zh: 牛德昌

translations.literal: Niu Dechang
translations.idiomatic: Niu Dechang

sentences.zh: 牛德昌，字彥欽，蔚州定安人。

translations.literal: Niu Dechang, courtesy name Yanqin, was a native of Ding'an in Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Dechang, styled Yanqin, came from Ding'an in Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父鐸，遼將作大監。

translations.literal: His father Duo was Director of Palace Construction under the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duo had been Director of Palace Construction under the Liao.

sentences.zh: 德昌少孤，其母教之學，有勸以就廕者，其母曰：「大監遺命不使作承奉也。」

translations.literal: Dechang was orphaned young; his mother had him study. When someone urged him to take a hereditary appointment, his mother said: "The Director left instructions that he was not to become a palace attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Dechang lost his father early; his mother had him pursue his studies. When someone urged him to take a hereditary post, his mother said, "The Director left word that he was never to become a palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 中皇統二年進士第，調礬山簿。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Huangtong of the Jin and was assigned as registrar of Fanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Huangtong and was posted as registrar of Fanshan.

sentences.zh: 遷萬泉令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 屬蒲、陝薦饑，群盜充斥，州縣城門晝閉。

translations.literal: At the time Pu and Shanxi were suffering famine; bandits swarmed everywhere, and the gates of prefectural and county cities were shut even by day.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Shanxi were in the grip of famine; bandits were everywhere, and prefectural and county gates stayed shut even in daylight.

sentences.zh: 德昌到官，即日開城門縱百姓出入，榜曰：「民苦饑寒，剽掠鄉聚以偷旦夕之命，甚可憐也。

translations.literal: When Dechang took office, that very day he opened the city gates and allowed the people to come and go freely. He posted a notice saying: "The people suffer from hunger and cold; they raid villages to steal a day's livelihood—this is deeply pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The day Dechang took office he opened the city gates and let the people move freely. He posted a notice: "The people are starving and freezing; they raid the countryside to scrape together another day of life—how pitiable that is.

sentences.zh: 能自新者一不問。」

translations.literal: Whoever can reform himself will not be questioned at all."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever is willing to mend his ways will not be questioned."

sentences.zh: 賊皆感激解散，縣境以安。

translations.literal: The bandits were all moved to gratitude and dispersed; the county borders became secure.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were moved by his words and dispersed, and the county returned to peace.

sentences.zh: 府尹王伯龍嘉之，禮待甚厚。

translations.literal: The prefect Wang Bolong commended him and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Wang Bolong praised him and treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 累官刑部、吏部侍郎，中都路都轉運使，廣甯、太原尹。

translations.literal: He rose through the posts of vice minister of justice, vice minister of personnel, director of transport for the Zhongdu circuit, and prefect of Guangning and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of vice minister of justice and personnel, director of transport for the Zhongdu circuit, and prefect of Guangning and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中奉大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 范承吉

translations.literal: Fan Chengji
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengji

sentences.zh: 范承吉，字寵之。

translations.literal: Fan Chengji, courtesy name Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengji, styled Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 好學問，屬遼季盜賊起，雖避地未嘗廢書。

translations.literal: He loved learning; when bandits rose in the late Liao, though he fled from place to place he never abandoned his books.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to learning; when bandits rose in the late Liao, he fled from place to place but never set his books aside.

sentences.zh: 天慶八年中進士丙科，授秘書省校書郎，至大定府金源令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianqing he passed the third rank of the civil service examination, was appointed collator in the Secretariat, and rose to magistrate of Jinyuan in Dading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianqing he passed the third rank of the jinshi examination, was appointed collator in the Secretariat, and eventually became magistrate of Jinyuan in Dading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歸朝為御前承應文字。

translations.literal: After submitting to the Jin court he served as a literary attendant before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted to the Jin he served as a literary attendant before the throne.

sentences.zh: 天會初，遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhui he was promoted to vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhui he was promoted to vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 四年，從攻太原，遷少府監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the attack on Taiyuan and was promoted to director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he accompanied the assault on Taiyuan and was promoted to director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 五年，宗翰克宋，所得金珠承吉司其出入，無毫髮欺，及還，犢車載書史而已，尋遷昭文館直學士，知絳州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zonghan conquered Song; Chengji supervised the receipt and disbursement of the gold and pearls taken, without the slightest fraud. When he returned, his ox-cart carried only books and records. Soon he was promoted to academician of the Zhaowen Hall and appointed prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zonghan conquered Song territory; Chengji oversaw the intake and disbursement of captured gold and pearls without a thread of dishonesty. On his return his ox-cart held nothing but books and records. He was soon made academician of the Zhaowen Hall and prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍興，民有為將士所掠而逃歸者，承吉使吏遍諭，俾其自實，凡數千人，具白元帥府，許自贖為良，或貧無貲者以公廚代輸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the army was mobilized, there were civilians who had been seized by soldiers and fled back home. Chengji had clerks go everywhere to announce that they should report themselves; several thousand in all did so. He reported fully to the marshal's headquarters, and they were permitted to ransom themselves back to commoner status; those too poor to pay had the cost covered from the public kitchen funds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the armies were in the field, civilians seized by soldiers had fled home. Chengji sent clerks throughout the district to announce that they should come forward and register; several thousand did. He reported the full list to the marshal's headquarters, and they were allowed to buy their way back to commoner status; those too poor to pay had the ransom covered from public funds.

sentences.zh: 六年，改河東北路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to transport commissioner of the Eastern Hebei North circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made transport commissioner of the Eastern Hebei North circuit.

sentences.zh: 時承宋季之弊，民賦繁重失當，承吉乃為經畫，立法簡便，所入增十數萬斛，官既足而民有餘。

translations.literal: At the time, inheriting the abuses of the late Song, the people's tax burdens were heavy and ill-apportioned. Chengji drew up a plan, established simple and convenient laws, and increased receipts by several hundred thousand bushels; the government was supplied and the people had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The district still bore the abuses of the late Song: tax burdens were crushing and poorly apportioned. Chengji reorganized the system with simple, workable rules and increased receipts by several hundred thousand bushels, so that the treasury was filled and the people still had something left.

sentences.zh: 曆同知平陽尹、西京副留守，遷河東南路轉運使，改同簽燕京留守事、順天軍節度使，屬地震壞民廬舍，有欲爭先營葺者，工匠過取其直，承吉命官屬董其役，先後以次，不間貧富，民賴以省費。

translations.literal: He served successively as deputy prefect of Pingyang, deputy guardian of the Western Capital, transport commissioner of the Eastern Hebei South circuit, co-signatory for the Yanjing garrison, and military commissioner of the Shuntian Army. When an earthquake destroyed the people's dwellings, those who wished to repair first were charged exorbitant prices by craftsmen. Chengji ordered his subordinates to supervise the work in sequence, rich and poor alike without distinction, and the people were thereby spared expense.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as deputy prefect of Pingyang, deputy guardian of the Western Capital, transport commissioner of the Eastern Hebei South circuit, co-signatory for the Yanjing garrison, and commissioner of the Shuntian circuit. After an earthquake wrecked people's homes, those who rushed to rebuild first were gouged by craftsmen. Chengji put his staff in charge of repairs in orderly sequence, without favoring rich over poor, and the people were spared ruinous costs.

sentences.zh: 曆鎮西軍節度使、行台禮部尚書、泰甯軍節度使，複鎮順天。

translations.literal: He served successively as military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army, minister of rites on the mobile secretariat, military commissioner of the Taining Army, and again commissioner of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as commissioner of the Zhenxi circuit, minister of rites on the mobile secretariat, commissioner of the Taining circuit, and again of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 奚卒散居境內，率數千人為盜，承吉繩以法不少貸，懼而不敢犯。

translations.literal: Xi soldiers were scattered throughout the territory, and in groups of several thousand became bandits. Chengji bound them with the law and showed no leniency; in fear they dared not offend.
translations.idiomatic: Xi soldiers scattered through his territory formed bands of thousands. Chengji enforced the law without mercy; they were afraid and dared not transgress.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，以光祿大夫致仕，卒年六十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he retired with the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan he retired as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 王政，辰州熊嶽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zheng was a native of Xiongyue in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zheng came from Xiongyue in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先仕渤海及遼，皆有顯者。

translations.literal: His ancestors who served Bohai and Liao had all achieved distinction.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears who served Bohai and Liao had all risen to prominence.

sentences.zh: 政當遼季亂，浮沈州裏。

translations.literal: Zheng lived through the turmoil at the end of Liao and drifted obscurely in his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng lived through the chaos at the end of Liao and kept a low profile in his home district.

sentences.zh: 高永昌據遼東，知政材略，欲用之。

translations.literal: When Gao Yongchang held Liaodong, recognizing Zheng's talent and strategy, he wished to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang held Liaodong, he recognized Zheng's ability and wanted to bring him into service.

sentences.zh: 政度其無成，辭謝不就。

translations.literal: Zheng judged that he would not succeed and declined, refusing the post.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng judged that Yongchang would not succeed and politely declined.

sentences.zh: 永昌敗，渤海人爭縛永昌以為功，政獨逡巡引退。

translations.literal: When Yongchang was defeated, the Bohai people vied to bind Yongchang to claim merit; Zheng alone hesitated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongchang fell, Bohai men scrambled to bind him up and claim credit; Zheng alone held back and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吳王闍母聞而異之，言于太祖，授盧州渤海軍謀克。

translations.literal: Prince Wu Zhamu heard of this and thought it remarkable; he spoke to the Founding Emperor, and Zheng was appointed company commander of the Bohai Army in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Zhamu heard of this and was struck by it; he spoke to the Founding Emperor, and Zheng was made company commander of the Bohai Army in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從破白嵆，下燕雲。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Baici and the conquest of Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaigns that broke Baici and took Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 及金兵伐宋，滑州降，留政為安撫使。

translations.literal: When the Jin army attacked Song, Huazhou surrendered, and Zheng was left behind as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies marched against Song, Huazhou surrendered, and Zheng was left behind as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 前此數州既降，複殺守將反為宋守，及是人以為政憂。

translations.literal: Previously several prefectures that had surrendered had again killed their garrison commanders and turned back to hold for Song; on this occasion people worried for Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Several prefectures that had already surrendered had killed their Jin garrison commanders and gone back over to Song, and now people feared for Zheng's life.

sentences.zh: 政曰：「苟利國家，雖死何避。」

translations.literal: Zheng said: "If it profits the state, what is there to fear in death?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "If it serves the state, why should I shrink from death?"

sentences.zh: 宋王宗望壯之，曰：「身沒王事，利及子孫，汝言是也。」

translations.literal: Prince Song Zongwang admired his spirit and said: "To die in the king's service brings benefit to one's descendants—your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Song Zongwang admired his resolve and said, "To die in the king's service brings reward to one's descendants—you speak truly."

sentences.zh: 政從數騎入州。

translations.literal: Zheng entered the prefecture with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng rode into the prefecture with only a few men.

sentences.zh: 是時，民多以饑為盜，坐系。

translations.literal: At that time many of the people had turned to banditry from hunger and were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people had turned to banditry out of hunger and sat in prison.

sentences.zh: 政皆釋之，發倉廩以賑貧乏，於是州民皆悅，不復叛。

translations.literal: Zheng released them all, opened the granaries to relieve the poor, and thereby the people of the prefecture were all pleased and did not rebel again.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng released them all, opened the granaries to feed the destitute, and the people of the prefecture were won over and did not rebel again.

sentences.zh: 傍郡聞之，亦多降者。

translations.literal: Neighboring prefectures heard of this, and many also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring prefectures heard of this, and many surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 宋王召政至轅門，撫其背曰：「吾以汝為死矣，乃複成功耶。」

translations.literal: Prince Song summoned Zheng to the camp gate, patted his back, and said: "I thought you were dead—yet you have succeeded again!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Song summoned Zheng to the camp gate, clapped him on the back, and said, "I thought you were dead—yet here you are, successful again!"

sentences.zh: 慰諭者久之。

translations.literal: He comforted and encouraged him at length.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted and praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 天會四年，為燕京都曲院同監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui he served as deputy supervisor of the capital wine bureau in Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianhui he was made deputy supervisor of the capital wine bureau in Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除同知金勝軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Jinsheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Jinsheng circuit.

sentences.zh: 改權侍衛親軍都指揮使、兼掌軍資。

translations.literal: He was changed to acting commander of the Palace Guard and concurrently managed military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting commander of the Palace Guard and concurrently managed military supplies.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍旅始定，管庫紀綱未立，掌吏皆因緣為奸。

translations.literal: At that time the army had only just been settled; regulations for the storehouses had not yet been established, and the clerks in charge all used the opportunity to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army had only just been pacified; storehouse regulations were not yet in place, and the clerks in charge all used the opening to commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 政獨明會計，嚴局鐍，金帛山積而出納無錙銖之失。

translations.literal: Zheng alone was skilled in accounting, strictly sealed the ledgers and locks, and though gold and silk piled up like mountains, receipts and disbursements were without the loss of a single cash.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng alone mastered the accounts, strictly sealed the ledgers, and though gold and silk piled up like mountains, not a single cash was lost in receipts or disbursements.

sentences.zh: 吳王闍母戲之曰：「汝為官久矣，而貧不加富何也？」

translations.literal: Prince Wu Zhamu jested with him and said: "You have been in office a long time—why does your poverty not turn to wealth?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Zhamu jested with him and said, "You have held office for years—why are you no richer?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「政以楊震四知自守，安得不貧。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Zheng keeps himself by Yang Zhen's Four Knowings—how could he not be poor?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zheng keeps himself by Yang Zhen's Four Knowings—how could I not be poor?"

sentences.zh: 吳王笑曰：「前言戲之耳。」

translations.literal: Prince Wu laughed and said: "My earlier words were only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu laughed and said, "What I said before was only a joke."

sentences.zh: 以黃金百兩、銀五百兩及所乘馬遺之。

translations.literal: He gave him one hundred taels of gold, five hundred taels of silver, and the horse he rode.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him one hundred taels of gold, five hundred taels of silver, and his own horse.

sentences.zh: 六年，授左監門將軍，曆安州刺史、檀州軍州事、戶吏房主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Left Gate General, and successively served as prefect of Anzhou, military prefect of Tanzhou, and chief clerk of the Household Registry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Left Gate General and successively served as prefect of Anzhou, military prefect of Tanzhou, and chief clerk of the Household Registry.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，遷保靜軍節度使，致仕卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he was transferred to military commissioner of the Baojing Army, retired, and died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan he was made military commissioner of the Baojing circuit, retired, and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 政本名南撒裏，嘗使高麗，因改名政。

translations.literal: Zheng's original name was Nansali; he had once been sent as envoy to Goryeo and therefore changed his name to Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's original name was Nansali; he had once been sent as envoy to Goryeo and took the name Zheng from that mission.

sentences.zh: 子遵仕、遵義、遵古。

translations.literal: His sons were Zunshi, Zunyi, and Zungu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zunshi, Zunyi, and Zungu.

sentences.zh: 遵古子庭筠有傳。

translations.literal: Zungu's son Tingyun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zungu's son Tingyun has his own biography elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 張奕，字彥微，其先澤州高平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Yanwei, was descended from Gaoping in Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, styled Yanwei, traced his ancestry to Gaoping in Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以廕補官，仕齊為歸德府通判。

translations.literal: He entered office through hereditary privilege and served Qi as vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through hereditary privilege and served the Qi state as vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，齊兵之在郡者二萬人謀為亂，約夜半舉燎相應。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was abolished, the twenty thousand Qi soldiers in the prefecture plotted rebellion, agreeing to raise beacon fires at midnight as signals to one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was abolished, the twenty thousand Qi troops still in the prefecture plotted a revolt, agreeing to light beacon fires at midnight as their signal.

sentences.zh: 奕知之，選市人丁壯授以兵，結陣扼其要巷，開小南門以示生路，亂不得作，比明亡匿略盡，擒其首惡誅之。

translations.literal: Yi learned of it, selected able-bodied men from the market and armed them, formed ranks to block the key alleys, and opened the Small South Gate to show an escape route. The rebellion could not break out; by dawn those in hiding had largely fled, and he seized the ringleaders and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi learned of the plot, drafted able-bodied men from the market and armed them, formed ranks to hold the key alleys, and opened the Small South Gate to offer an escape route. The revolt never broke out; by dawn most of the conspirators had fled, and Yi seized the ringleaders and executed them.

sentences.zh: 後五日，都統完顏阿魯補以軍至歸德，欲根株餘黨，奕以闔門保郡人無他，遂止。

translations.literal: Five days later the commander Wanyan Alubu arrived at Guide with his army and wished to root out the remaining conspirators. Yi pledged his entire household that the people of the prefecture had no further designs, and the pursuit was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Commander Wanyan Alubu arrived at Guide with his army and wanted to root out every last conspirator. Yi pledged his entire household that the people of the prefecture meant no further harm, and the purge was stopped.

sentences.zh: 行台承制除同知歸德尹。

translations.literal: The mobile secretariat, acting under imperial commission, appointed him deputy prefect of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: The mobile secretariat, acting under imperial commission, appointed him deputy prefect of Guide.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，以河南與宋，改同知沂州防禦使事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan, when Henan was ceded to Song, he was changed to deputy defender of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan, when Henan was ceded to Song, he was made deputy defender of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，宗弼複取河南，征奕赴行省，既定汴京，授汴京副留守。

translations.literal: In the third year Zongbi recovered Henan; Yi was summoned to the mobile secretariat, and once Bianjing was secured he was appointed deputy guardian of Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zongbi retook Henan; Yi was summoned to the mobile secretariat, and once Bianjing was secured he was made deputy guardian of Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 曆陳、秦州防禦使，同知太原尹。

translations.literal: He successively served as defender of Chen and Qin prefectures and as deputy metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as defender of Chen and Qin prefectures and as deputy metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉甯軍報夏人侵界，詔奕往征之。

translations.literal: The Jinning Army reported that the Xia had invaded the border; an edict ordered Yi to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinning Army reported a Xia border incursion; the throne ordered Yi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 奕至境上，按籍各歸所侵土，還奏曰：「折氏世守麟府，以抗夏人。

translations.literal: Yi reached the border, checked the registers, and returned each tract of invaded land; returning he memorialized: "The Zhe clan for generations held Lin Prefecture to resist the Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reached the border, checked the registers, and restored each tract of invaded land; on returning he memorialized, "The Zhe clan had held Lin Prefecture for generations to resist the Xia.

sentences.zh: 本朝有其地遂以與夏。

translations.literal: Our dynasty possessed that territory and then gave it to the Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty held that territory and then ceded it to the Xia.

sentences.zh: 夏人夷折氏墳壟而戮其屍，折氏怨入骨髓而不得報也。

translations.literal: The Xia leveled the Zhe clan's tombs and desecrated their corpses; the Zhe clan's hatred entered to the marrow and could not be avenged.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia leveled the Zhe tombs and desecrated their dead; the Zhe clan's hatred ran to the marrow and could not be avenged.

sentences.zh: 今複使守晉寧，故激怒夏人使為鼠侵，而條上其罪，苟欲開邊釁以雪私仇耳。

translations.literal: Now they are again made to guard Jinning, so the Xia are deliberately provoked into petty incursions, and charges are listed against them—this is merely to open a border quarrel and settle a private grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are posted again to guard Jinning, deliberately provoking petty Xia raids while charges are filed against them—this is only to open a border quarrel and settle a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 獨可徙折氏他郡，則夏人自安。」

translations.literal: They need only be moved to another prefecture, and the Xia will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Move the Zhe clan to another prefecture, and the Xia will settle down of themselves."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之，遂移折氏守青州。

translations.literal: The court adopted this and thereupon transferred the Zhe clan to guard Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and transferred the Zhe clan to guard Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 正隆間，同知西京留守事，遷河東北路轉運使。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong era he served as deputy guardian of the Western Capital and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong North Route.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenglong he served as deputy guardian of the Western Capital and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong North Route.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，征為戶部尚書，甫視事，得疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was summoned as minister of revenue; he had only just taken office when he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was summoned as minister of revenue; he had barely taken office when he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 李瞻，薊州玉田人。

translations.literal: Li Zhan was a native of Yutian in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhan came from Yutian in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遼天慶二年進士，為平州望雲令。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Tianqing of Liao and served as magistrate of Wangyun in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqing under the Liao and became magistrate of Wangyun in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張覺據平州叛，以瞻從事。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jue held Ping Prefecture in rebellion, he employed Zhan on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jue seized Ping Prefecture in rebellion, he took Zhan onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 宗望複平州，覺亡去，城中複叛，瞻逾城出降，其子不能出，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Zongwang recovered Ping Prefecture; Jue fled, the city rebelled again, and Zhan climbed over the wall to surrender. His son could not get out and was killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang retook Ping Prefecture; Jue fled, the city rose again, and Zhan climbed over the wall to surrender. His son could not escape and was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 宋王宗望嘉之。

translations.literal: Prince Song Zongwang commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Song Zongwang praised him.

sentences.zh: 承制以為興平府判官。

translations.literal: Acting under imperial commission, he was appointed judicial administrator of Xingping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Acting under imperial commission, he was appointed judicial administrator of Xingping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，遷大理少卿，從宗望南伐，為漢軍糧料使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, followed Zongwang on the southern campaign, and served as grain commissioner for the Han armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhui he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, accompanied Zongwang on the southern campaign, and served as grain commissioner for the Han armies.

sentences.zh: 四年，金兵圍汴，宋人請割河北三鎮，瞻與禮部侍郎李天翼安撫河北東、西兩路，略定懷、浚、衛等州，衛、湯陰等縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Jin army besieged Bian; the Song requested to cede the three prefectures of Hebei. Zhan, together with Vice Minister of Rites Li Tianyi, pacified the Eastern and Western circuits of Hebei and brought under control the prefectures of Huai, Jun, Wei, and others, and the counties of Wei, Tangyin, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Jin armies besieged Bianliang; the Song asked to cede the three Hebei prefectures. Zhan and Vice Minister of Rites Li Tianyi pacified the Eastern and Western Hebei circuits and secured the prefectures of Huai, Jun, Wei, and others, along with counties such as Wei and Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 七年，知寧州，累遷德州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed prefect of Ningzhou and was eventually promoted to defender of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made prefect of Ningzhou and eventually rose to defender of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 為政寬平，民懷其惠，相率詣京師請留者數百千人。

translations.literal: His governance was mild and even-handed; the people cherished his kindness, and several hundred or a thousand went in groups to the capital to request that he be kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and fair; the people cherished his kindness, and several hundred of them went together to the capital to ask that he be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，遷濟州路轉運使，改忠順軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was promoted to transport commissioner of the Jizhou circuit and transferred to military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was made transport commissioner of the Jizhou circuit and then commissioner of the Zhongshun circuit.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，盜賊蜂起，瞻增築城壘為備，蔚人賴之以安。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong bandits swarmed forth; Zhan strengthened the city walls and ramparts as a precaution, and the people of Yu relied on this for security.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenglong reign bandits rose everywhere; Zhan strengthened the walls and ramparts as a precaution, and the people of Yu relied on his preparations for their safety.

sentences.zh: 大定初，卒於官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading reign he died in office.

sentences.zh: 劉敏行

translations.literal: Liu Minxing
translations.idiomatic: Liu Minxing

sentences.zh: 劉敏行，平州人。

translations.literal: Liu Minxing was a native of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Minxing came from Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登天會三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the third year of Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Tianhui.

sentences.zh: 除太子校書郎，累遷肥鄉令。

translations.literal: He was appointed collator to the Crown Prince and was eventually promoted to magistrate of Feixiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed collator to the Crown Prince and eventually became magistrate of Feixiang.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，盜賊掠人為食。

translations.literal: That year there was severe famine; bandits seized people for food.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine was severe, and bandits seized people for food.

sentences.zh: 諸縣老弱入保郡城，不敢耕種，農事廢，畎畝荒蕪。

translations.literal: The elderly and weak of the various counties entered the walled refuge of the prefectural city and dared not farm; agriculture was abandoned and the fields lay waste.
translations.idiomatic: The elderly and weak from the surrounding counties fled into the walled refuge of the prefectural city and dared not farm; agriculture collapsed and the fields lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 敏行白州，借軍士三十護縣民出耕，多張旗幟為疑兵，敏行率軍巡邏，日暮則閱民入城，由是盜不敢犯而耕稼滋殖。

translations.literal: Minxing reported to the prefecture, borrowed thirty soldiers to escort the county people out to farm, set up many banners as a decoy force, led the troops on patrol himself, and at dusk reviewed the people back into the city. Thereby the bandits dared not attack, and cultivation flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: Minxing appealed to the prefecture, borrowed thirty soldiers to escort the county people out to the fields, set up many banners to suggest a larger force, led patrols himself, and at dusk reviewed everyone back inside the walls. The bandits dared not strike, and farming revived.

sentences.zh: 轉高平令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 縣城圮壞久不修，大盜橫恣，掠縣鎮不能禦。

translations.literal: The county walls had long lain in ruins without repair; great bandits ran rampant, plundering the county seat and its towns without anyone able to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The county walls had long been in ruins and unrepaired; major bandits ran wild, raiding the county seat and its towns with no one able to stop them.

sentences.zh: 敏行出己俸，率僚吏出錢顧役繕治，百姓欣然從之，凡用二千人，版築遂完。

translations.literal: Minxing contributed his own salary, led the subordinate officials in putting up money to hire labor for repairs, and the people gladly followed; two thousand men in all were employed, and the rammed-earth walls were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Minxing paid from his own salary, led his staff in contributing funds to hire labor for repairs, and the people gladly joined in; two thousand workers were employed, and the rammed-earth fortifications were completed.

sentences.zh: 鄉村百姓入保，賊至不能犯。

translations.literal: Villagers and common people entered the walled refuge; when bandits came they could not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers took refuge inside the walls, and when bandits came they could not break in.

sentences.zh: 凡九遷，為河北東路轉運使。

translations.literal: In all he was promoted nine times and became transport commissioner of the Hebei East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In all he was promoted nine times and became transport commissioner of the Hebei East circuit.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 傅慎微

translations.literal: Fu Shenwei
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shenwei

sentences.zh: 傅慎微，字幾先。

translations.literal: Fu Shenwei, courtesy name Jixian.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shenwei, styled Jixian.

sentences.zh: 其先秦州沙溪人，後徙建昌。

translations.literal: His ancestors were from Shaxi in Qin Prefecture and later moved to Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from Shaxi in Qin Prefecture and later moved to Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 慎微遷居長安。

translations.literal: Shenwei moved his residence to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwei made his home in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 宋末登進士，累官河東路經制使。

translations.literal: At the end of Song he passed the civil service examination and rose to commissioner for the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Song he passed the jinshi examination and eventually became commissioner for the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 宗翰已克汴京，使婁室定陝西，慎微率眾迎戰，兵敗被獲，送至元帥府。

translations.literal: Zonghan had already taken Bianjing and sent Loushi to secure Shaanxi; Shenwei led his forces to meet the attack, was defeated and captured, and was sent to the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Zonghan took Bianliang he sent Loushi to secure Shaanxi; Shenwei led his troops out to fight, was defeated and captured, and was sent to the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元帥宗翰愛其才學，弗殺，羈置歸化州，希尹收置門下。

translations.literal: Marshal Zonghan admired his talent and learning and did not kill him; he was detained at Guihua Prefecture, and Xiyin took him into his household.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Zonghan admired his learning and spared his life; he was held at Guihua Prefecture, and Xiyin took him into his household.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複取河南地，起為陝西經略使，尋權同州節度使事。

translations.literal: When Zongbi recovered the Henan territory, Shenwei was recalled as commissioner of the Shaanxi frontier and soon acted as military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi retook Henan, Shenwei was recalled as Shaanxi frontier commissioner and soon acted as military commissioner of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，陝西大旱，饑死者十七八，以慎微為京兆、鄜延、環慶三路經濟使，許以便宜。

translations.literal: The next year Shaanxi suffered severe drought; seven or eight out of ten died of famine. Shenwei was appointed economic commissioner for the three circuits of Jingzhao, Fuyan, and Huanqing, with discretionary authority granted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shaanxi was stricken by drought; seven or eight out of ten starved to death. Shenwei was made economic commissioner for the Jingzhao, Fuyan, and Huanqing circuits, with authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 慎微募民入粟，得二十余萬石，立養濟院飼餓者，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Shenwei recruited the people to contribute grain and obtained more than two hundred thousand bushels; he established relief houses to feed the starving, and a great many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwei urged the people to bring in grain and collected more than two hundred thousand bushels; he set up relief houses to feed the starving, and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 改同知京兆尹，權陝西諸路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy prefect of Jingzhao and acted as transport commissioner for the various Shaanxi circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy prefect of Jingzhao and acted as transport commissioner for the Shaanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 複修三白、龍首等渠以溉田，募民屯種，貸牛及種子以濟之，民賴其利。

translations.literal: He restored the Sanbai, Longshou, and other canals to irrigate the fields, recruited the people for garrison farming, and lent oxen and seed to support them; the people relied on this for their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Sanbai, Longshou, and other canals to irrigate the fields, recruited settlers for garrison farming, and lent oxen and seed; the people prospered from his efforts.

sentences.zh: 轉中京副留守，用廉，改忻州刺史，累遷太常卿，除定武軍節度使，移靜難軍，忤用事者，蘇保衡救之得免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy guardian of the Central Capital; on account of integrity he was made prefect of Xinzhou, was eventually promoted to minister of imperial sacrifices, appointed military commissioner of the Dingwu Army, and transferred to the Jingnan Army. He offended those in power, but Su Baoheng rescued him and he escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy guardian of the Central Capital; recognized for integrity he was made prefect of Xinzhou, rose to minister of imperial sacrifices, was commissioner of the Dingwu circuit, then of Jingnan. He offended those in power, but Su Baoheng intervened and he escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 大定初，複為太常卿，遷禮部尚書，與翰林侍講學士徒單子溫、翰林待制移剌熙載俱兼同修國史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he again became minister of imperial sacrifices, was promoted to minister of rites, and together with Hanlin Lecturer Tushan Ziwen and Hanlin Attendant Yila Xizai was concurrently appointed to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he again became minister of imperial sacrifices, then minister of rites, and together with Hanlin Lecturer Tushan Ziwen and Hanlin Attendant Yila Xizai was appointed to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 慎微博學喜著書，嘗奏《興亡金鏡錄》一百卷。

translations.literal: Shenwei was broadly learned and loved to write books; he once presented to the throne the "Records of Rise and Fall, Mirror of Gold" in one hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwei was widely learned and fond of writing; he once presented to the throne his hundred-volume Records of Rise and Fall, Mirror of Gold.

sentences.zh: 性純質，篤古喜談兵，時人以為迂闊雲。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and plain; he was devoted to antiquity and loved to discuss military affairs; people of the time considered him impractical and broad-brushed.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and upright by nature, devoted to antiquity and fond of military talk; contemporaries thought him impractical and wide of the mark.

sentences.zh: 劉煥，字德文，中山人。

translations.literal: Liu Huan, courtesy name Dewen, was a native of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan, styled Dewen, came from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 宋末起兵，城中久乏食，煥尚幼，煮糠核而食之，自飲其清者，以醲厚者供其母，鄉里異之。

translations.literal: At the end of Song, when troops were raised, the city long lacked food; Huan was still young, boiled chaff and husks to eat, drank the thin liquid himself, and gave the thick portion to his mother—the village thought this remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were raised at the end of Song, the city long lacked food; Huan was still young, boiled chaff and husks to eat, drank the thin broth himself, and gave the thick portion to his mother—neighbors marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 稍長就學，天寒擁糞火讀書不怠。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older he took up study; in cold weather he huddled over a dung fire and read without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he took up study; in cold weather he huddled over a dung fire and read without slackening.

sentences.zh: 登天德元年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the first year of Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 調任丘尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as sheriff of Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned sheriff of Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 縣令貪污，煥每規正之，秩滿，令持杯酒謝曰：「尉廉慎，使我獲考。」

translations.literal: The magistrate was corrupt; Huan constantly admonished him. When his term ended the magistrate held a cup of wine and thanked him, saying: "Sheriff, your integrity and caution enabled me to pass inspection."
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was corrupt; Huan constantly corrected him. When his term ended the magistrate raised a cup and thanked him, saying, "Sheriff, your integrity and caution let me pass inspection."

sentences.zh: 調中都市令。

translations.literal: He was assigned as market magistrate of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed market magistrate of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 樞密使僕散忽土家有絛結工，牟利於市，不肯從市籍役，煥系之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pusan Hutu had a cord-knotting craftsman in his household who profited in the market and refused to submit to market registration and corvée; Huan seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Pusan Hutu had a cord-knotting craftsman in his household who profited in the market and refused market registration and corvée; Huan seized him.

sentences.zh: 忽土召煥，煥不往，暴工罪而笞之。

translations.literal: Hutu summoned Huan, but Huan did not go; he publicly declared the craftsman's crimes and had him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu summoned Huan, but Huan did not go; he publicly declared the craftsman's crimes and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 煥初除市令，過謝鄉人吏部侍郎石琚，琚不悅曰：「京師浩穰，不與外郡同，棄簡就煩，吾所不曉也。」

translations.literal: When Huan was first appointed market magistrate he went to thank his fellow townsman, Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Ju; Ju was displeased and said: "The capital is vast and crowded, unlike outer prefectures—to abandon ease for trouble is what I cannot understand."
translations.idiomatic: When Huan was first appointed market magistrate he went to thank his fellow townsman, Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Ju; Ju was displeased and said, "The capital is vast and crowded, unlike outer prefectures—to trade ease for trouble is beyond me."

sentences.zh: 至是，始重之。

translations.literal: Only then did he come to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Ju come to respect him.

sentences.zh: 以廉升京兆推官，再遷北京警巡使。

translations.literal: On account of integrity he was promoted to investigating censor of Jingzhao and later to patrol commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity he was promoted to investigating censor of Jingzhao and later to patrol commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 捕二惡少杖于庭中，戒之曰：「孝弟敬慎，則為君子。

translations.literal: He seized two vicious youths and flogged them in the courtyard, admonishing them: "With filial piety, brotherly respect, reverence, and caution, one becomes a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He seized two vicious youths and flogged them in the courtyard, warning them, "Filial piety, brotherly respect, reverence, and caution make a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 暴戾隱賊，則為小人。

translations.literal: With violence, cruelty, concealment, and treachery, one becomes a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Violence, cruelty, concealment, and treachery make a petty man.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，毋狃于故習，國有明罰，吾不得私也。」

translations.literal: From now on do not cling to your old habits; the state has clear punishments, and I cannot show favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: From now on do not cling to your old ways; the state has clear punishments, and I cannot show favoritism."

sentences.zh: 自是，眾皆畏憚，毋敢犯者。

translations.literal: From then on all feared and respected him, and none dared to offend.
translations.idiomatic: From then on everyone feared him, and none dared to transgress.

sentences.zh: 召為監察禦使，父老數百人或臥車下，或挽其靴鐙，曰：「我欲複留使君期年，不可得也。」

translations.literal: When he was summoned as supervising censor, several hundred elders either lay beneath his carriage or pulled at his boot stirrups, saying: "We wished to keep the commissioner for another year, but it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned as supervising censor, several hundred elders lay beneath his carriage or clutched his stirrups, saying, "We wanted to keep you for another year, but we cannot."

sentences.zh: 以本官攝戶部員外郎，代州錢監雜青銅鑄錢，錢色惡，類鐵錢。

translations.literal: Acting in his present office as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, the Dai Prefecture mint mixed bronze with other metals to cast coin; the coin was poor in quality and resembled iron money.
translations.idiomatic: Acting as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, he found that the Dai Prefecture mint was alloying bronze to cast coin; the coins were poor in quality and looked like iron cash.

sentences.zh: 民間盜鑄，抵罪者眾，朝廷患之，下尚書省議。

translations.literal: The people counterfeited in secret; many were punished. The court was troubled and referred the matter to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting spread among the people and many were punished; the court was alarmed and referred the matter to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 煥奏曰：「錢寶純用黃銅精治之，中濡以錫，若青銅可鑄，歷代無緣不用。

translations.literal: Huan memorialized: "Precious coin should be made purely of yellow copper finely refined, with tin infused within. If bronze alloy could be used for casting, no dynasty through the ages would have failed to use it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan memorialized, "Standard coin should be cast from pure yellow copper finely refined, with tin worked in. If bronze alloy were acceptable, no dynasty in history would have done without it.

sentences.zh: 自代州取二分與四六分，青黃雜糅，務省銅而功易就。

translations.literal: From Dai Prefecture they take two parts and four-six parts, mixing green and yellow, striving to save copper while making the work easy to complete.
translations.idiomatic: At Dai they mix two parts with four-six parts, blending alloys to save copper and finish the work quickly.

sentences.zh: 由是，民間盜鑄，陷罪者眾，非朝廷意也。

translations.literal: Because of this, counterfeiting spread among the people and many were trapped in crime—this was not the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, counterfeiting spread and many were condemned—this was not what the court intended.

sentences.zh: 必欲為天下利，宜純用黃銅，得數少而利遠。

translations.literal: If one truly wishes to benefit the realm, one should use pure yellow copper alone; though the quantity obtained is less, the profit extends far.
translations.idiomatic: If the realm is to benefit, coin should be cast from pure yellow copper alone; the yield may be smaller, but the long-term gain is greater.

sentences.zh: 其新錢已流行者，宜驗數輸納准換。」

translations.literal: As for the new coin already in circulation, the quantity should be verified, surrendered, and exchanged at standard value."
translations.idiomatic: As for the debased coin already in circulation, holders should surrender it by count and receive standard coin in exchange."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 再遷管州刺史，耆老數百人疏其著跡十一事，詣節鎮請留煥，曰：「刺史守職奉法，乞留之。」

translations.literal: He was again promoted to prefect of Guanzhou; several hundred elders submitted a memorial listing eleven of his achievements and went to the military commissioner to request that Huan be kept, saying: "The prefect observes his duties and upholds the law—we beg that he be retained."
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to prefect of Guanzhou; several hundred elders listed eleven of his achievements and petitioned the military commissioner to keep Huan, saying, "The prefect serves dutifully and upholds the law—we beg you to retain him."

sentences.zh: 以廉升鄭州防禦使，遷官一階，轉同知北京留守事。

translations.literal: On account of integrity he was promoted to defender of Zhengzhou, advanced one rank in office, and transferred to deputy guardian of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity he was made defender of Zhengzhou, advanced one rank, and transferred to deputy guardian of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸上京，所過州郡大發民夫治橋樑馳道，以希恩賞，煥所部惟平治端好而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong visited the Upper Capital, the prefectures and counties along the route conscripted masses of laborers to repair bridges and imperial highways in hope of reward; in Huan's jurisdiction they merely leveled and made things properly passable.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong visited the Upper Capital, every prefecture along the route conscripted masses of laborers to rebuild bridges and highways in hope of reward; in Huan's district they merely leveled the roads to make them properly passable.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其意，遷遼東路轉運使，卒。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his intent and promoted him to transport commissioner of the Liaodong circuit; he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his restraint and made him transport commissioner of the Liaodong circuit; he died.

sentences.zh: 高昌福

translations.literal: Gao Changfu
translations.idiomatic: Gao Changfu

sentences.zh: 高昌福，中都宛平人。

translations.literal: Gao Changfu was a native of Wanping in the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Changfu came from Wanping in the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 父履，遼御史中丞致仕，太宗聞其名召之，未及入見而卒，特詔昌福釋服應舉。

translations.literal: His father Lü was a retired vice censor-in-chief of Liao; Emperor Taizong heard his name and summoned him, but before he could enter audience he died. A special edict allowed Changfu to leave mourning and sit for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lü had retired as vice censor-in-chief under the Liao; Emperor Taizong heard of him and summoned him, but he died before he could appear at court. A special edict allowed Changfu to leave mourning and sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 登天會十年進士第，補樞密院令史。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the tenth year of Tianhui and was appointed clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Tianhui and was appointed clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，辟元帥府令史。

translations.literal: The next year he was recruited as clerk in the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recruited as clerk in the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 皇統初，宗弼複河南，元帥府治汴，人有疑似被獲，皆目為宋諜者，即殺之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangtong, Zongbi recovered Henan and the marshal's headquarters was stationed at Bian; anyone seized on suspicion was labeled a Song spy and immediately killed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huangtong, Zongbi retook Henan and the marshal's headquarters was at Bian; anyone seized on suspicion was called a Song spy and killed at once.

sentences.zh: 昌福讞得其實，釋去者甚眾。

translations.literal: Changfu investigated and obtained the facts; a great many were released.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu investigated the cases and established the facts; a great many were released.

sentences.zh: 許州都統韓常用法嚴，好殺人，遣介送囚於汴，或道亡，監吏自度失囚恐得罪，欲盡殺諸囚以滅口。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou commander Han Chang enforced the law harshly and loved to kill; he sent escorts to deliver prisoners to Bian, and sometimes prisoners escaped on the road. The supervising clerks, judging that they would be punished for losing prisoners, wished to kill all the prisoners to silence witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Han Chang of Xuzhou enforced the law harshly and was fond of executions; he sent escorts to deliver prisoners to Bian, and sometimes prisoners escaped en route. The escort officers, fearing punishment for the loss, wanted to kill all the prisoners to cover their tracks.

sentences.zh: 昌福識監吏意，窮竟其狀，免死者十七八，而諸吏遂怨昌福，欲構害之。

translations.literal: Changfu perceived the clerks' intent, investigated the matter thoroughly, and spared seven or eight out of ten from death; the clerks then resented Changfu and wished to frame him for harm.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu saw what the officers intended, investigated thoroughly, and spared seven or eight out of ten; the officers then resented him and plotted to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 是時方用兵，梁、楚間夜多陰雨，元帥府選人偵宋兵動靜，諸吏遣昌福。

translations.literal: At that time the armies were engaged; between Liang and Chu the nights were often rainy. The marshal's headquarters chose men to spy on Song troop movements, and the clerks sent Changfu.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were then in the field; between Liang and Chu the nights were often rainy. The marshal's headquarters needed scouts to watch Song movements, and the clerks sent Changfu.

sentences.zh: 昌福不辭即行，盡得敵軍虛實報元帥府。

translations.literal: Changfu made no excuse and set out at once, obtained full knowledge of the enemy's strength and weakness, and reported to the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Changfu set out without hesitation, learned the enemy's full disposition, and reported back to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師還，除震武軍節度副使，轉行台禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed deputy military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and transferred to vice director of rites on the mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made deputy commissioner of the Zhenwu circuit and vice director of rites on the mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天德間，行台罷，改絳陽軍節度副使，入為兵部員外郎，改河間少尹。

translations.literal: During the Tiande era the mobile secretariat was abolished; he was transferred to deputy military commissioner of the Jiangyang Army, entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of War, and was made junior prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiande the mobile secretariat was abolished; he became deputy commissioner of the Jiangyang circuit, entered the capital as vice director of the Ministry of War, and was made junior prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，上書陳便宜事，上披閱再三，因謂侍臣曰：「內外官皆上書言事，可以知人材優劣，不然，朕何由知之。」

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Changfu submitted a memorial setting forth practical measures; the emperor read it repeatedly and then said to his attendants: "When officials inside and outside all submit memorials on affairs of state, one can know the superior and inferior among talents—otherwise, how would I know them?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne, Changfu submitted a memorial on practical measures; the emperor read it repeatedly and told his attendants, "When officials everywhere submit memorials, one can judge talent—otherwise, how would I know?"

sentences.zh: 三除同知東京留守事，治最，遷山東西路轉運使、工部尚書，改彰德軍節度使。

translations.literal: Three times he was appointed deputy guardian of the Eastern Capital; his administration ranked highest, and he was promoted to transport commissioner of the Shandong West Route and minister of works, then changed to military commissioner of the Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he was appointed deputy guardian of the Eastern Capital; his administration ranked highest, and he was promoted to transport commissioner of the Shandong West Route and minister of works, then made military commissioner of the Zhangde circuit.

sentences.zh: 上書言賦稅太重，上問翰林學士張景仁曰：「稅法比近代為輕，而以為重何也？」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying the land tax was too heavy. The emperor asked Hanlin Academician Zhang Jingren: "The tax law is lighter than in recent times—why is it thought heavy?"
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that land taxes were too heavy. The emperor asked Hanlin Academician Zhang Jingren, "The tax code is lighter than in recent times—why does he think it heavy?"

sentences.zh: 景仁曰：「今之稅殊輕，若複輕之，國用且不足。」

translations.literal: Jingren said: "Today's tax is already quite light; if it were lightened further, state revenue would be insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Jingren said, "Today's taxes are already quite light; lighten them further and state revenue will fall short."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 累遷河中尹，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was eventually promoted to metropolitan prefect of Hezhong, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to metropolitan prefect of Hezhong, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 孫德淵，字資深，興中府人也。

translations.literal: Sun Deyuan, courtesy name Zishen, was a native of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deyuan, styled Zishen, came from Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大定十六年進士，調石州軍事判官、淶水丞，察廉遷沙河令。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the sixteenth year of Dading, was assigned as military judicial administrator of Shizhou and assistant magistrate of Laishui, and on account of integrity was promoted to magistrate of Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Dading, served as military judicial administrator of Shizhou and assistant magistrate of Laishui, and was promoted to magistrate of Shahe for integrity.

sentences.zh: 有盜秋桑者，主逐捕之，盜以叉自刺其足面，曰：「秋桑例不禁采，汝何得刺我？」

translations.literal: There was a thief who stole autumn mulberry leaves; the owner pursued and seized him. The thief stabbed his own foot and face with a fork and said: "Autumn mulberry leaves are by custom not forbidden to gather—how can you stab me?"
translations.idiomatic: A thief was caught stealing autumn mulberry leaves; the owner pursued him. The thief stabbed his own foot and face with a fork and cried, "Autumn mulberry leaves are customarily free to gather—how dare you wound me?"

sentences.zh: 主懼，賂而求免，盜不從，訴之縣。

translations.literal: The owner was afraid, offered a bribe to be let off, but the thief refused and brought suit at the county.
translations.idiomatic: The owner was frightened, offered a bribe to settle the matter, but the thief refused and sued at the county yamen.

sentences.zh: 德淵曰：「若逐捕而傷，瘡必在後，今在前，乃自刺也。」

translations.literal: Deyuan said: "If wounded while being pursued and seized, the wounds would be on the back; now they are on the front—he stabbed himself."
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan said, "Wounds from pursuit would be on the back; these are on the front—he stabbed himself."

sentences.zh: 盜遂引服。

translations.literal: The thief then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The thief then confessed.

sentences.zh: 選尚書省令史，不就。

translations.literal: He was selected as clerk in the Ministry of Revenue but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去官，民為刻石祠之。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning was over he left office; the people carved a stone stele in his shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father; the people erected a stone stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 察廉，起複北京轉運司都勾判官，以累薦遷中都左警巡使、監察御史、山東東路轉運副使，累官大理丞、兼左拾遺。

translations.literal: On account of integrity he was recalled to serve as chief investigating clerk of the Northern Capital transport office; through repeated recommendations he was promoted to left patrol commissioner of the Central Capital, supervising censor, deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong East circuit, and eventually reached the posts of vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and concurrent left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity he was recalled as chief investigating clerk of the Northern Capital transport office; through repeated recommendations he rose to left patrol commissioner of the Central Capital, supervising censor, deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong East circuit, and eventually vice director of the Court of Judicial Review with concurrent appointment as left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 審官院奏德淵剛正幹能，可任繁劇，遂再任。

translations.literal: The Bureau for Review of Appointments reported that Deyuan was upright, firm, and capable, fit for heavy duties, and he was therefore given a second term.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau for Review of Appointments reported that Deyuan was upright and capable of heavy duties, and he was given a second term.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除特遷恩州刺史，入為右司郎中，滕州刺史，遷同知河間府事，曆大興治中、同知府事。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning was completed and his term of service ended, he was specially promoted to prefect of Enzhou, entered the capital as director of the right bureau, became prefect of Tengzhou, was promoted to deputy prefect of Hejian Prefecture, and served successively as administrative aide of Daxing and deputy prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he was specially promoted to prefect of Enzhou, entered the capital as director of the right bureau, became prefect of Tengzhou, deputy prefect of Hejian, and served in turn as administrative aide of Daxing and deputy prefect.

sentences.zh: 大安初，遷盤安軍節度使，改河北西路按察轉運使，改昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was promoted to military commissioner of the Pan'an Army, transferred to inspector and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit, and changed to military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Da'an he was commissioner of the Pan'an circuit, then inspector and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit, then commissioner of the Zhaoyi circuit.

sentences.zh: 潞州破被執，俄有拜於前者，皆沙河舊民也，密護德淵，由是得脫。

translations.literal: When Luzhou fell he was captured; soon men came forward to bow before him—all were old subjects from Shahe—and they secretly protected Deyuan, whereby he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou fell he was taken prisoner; soon men came forward to bow to him—all were his old subjects from Shahe—and they secretly protected him until he escaped.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，拜工部尚書，攝御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was appointed minister of works and acted as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was made minister of works and acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東乏兵食，有司請鬻恩例舉人，居喪者亦許納錢就試。

translations.literal: At that time Shandong lacked provisions for the army; the authorities requested to sell honorary examination candidacies, and even those in mourning were permitted to pay money and sit for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong then lacked army provisions; the authorities proposed selling honorary examination candidacies, and even those in mourning would be allowed to pay and sit for the exam.

sentences.zh: 德淵奏，此大傷名教，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Deyuan memorialized that this gravely harmed the norms of teaching and propriety; the matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan memorialized that this would gravely harm moral teaching; the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired.

sentences.zh: 監察御史許古論德淵「忠亮明敏，可以大用，近許告老，士大夫竊歎，望朝廷起複，必能建明以利國家。」

translations.literal: Supervising censor Xu Gu discussed Deyuan: "Loyal, bright, clear, and keen—he can be greatly employed. Recently he has been permitted to retire; the scholar-officials sigh in private. It is hoped the court will recall him; he will surely be able to set forth enlightened policies to benefit the state."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Xu Gu wrote of Deyuan, "Loyal, upright, and keen—he is fit for great responsibility. He has lately been allowed to retire, and scholars sigh in private. The court should recall him; he would surely advance policies to benefit the state."

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉納。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong praised and accepted the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 未及用而卒。

translations.literal: Before he could be employed he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could be recalled he died.

sentences.zh: 趙鑒，字擇善，濟南章丘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jian, courtesy name Zeshan, was a native of Zhangqiu in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jian, styled Zeshan, came from Zhangqiu in Jinan.

sentences.zh: 宋建炎二年進士，調廬州司理參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Jianyan of Song and was assigned as judicial administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jianyan under Song and was posted as judicial administrator of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時江、淮方用兵，鑒棄官還鄉里。

translations.literal: At that time the Yangzi and Huai regions were at war; Jian abandoned his post and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi and Huai regions were then at war; Jian resigned his post and returned home.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，除曆城丞，轉長清令，皆劇邑難治，鑒政甚著。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established he was appointed assistant magistrate of Licheng and transferred to magistrate of Changqing—both were difficult districts to govern, and Jian's administration was highly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was established he was assistant magistrate of Licheng and then magistrate of Changqing—both were notoriously difficult posts, and Jian's governance was outstanding.

sentences.zh: 劉豫召見，遷直秘閣、提舉涇原路弓箭手、兼提點本路刑獄公事，誡之曰：「邊將多不法，可痛繩之。」

translations.literal: Liu Yu summoned him for audience, promoted him to direct access to the Secret Repository, commissioner for archers of the Jingyuan circuit, and concurrent commissioner for criminal affairs of the circuit, admonishing him: "The frontier generals are often lawless—you may punish them severely."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu summoned him, made him direct access to the Secret Repository, commissioner for archers of the Jingyuan circuit, and concurrent commissioner for criminal affairs, warning him, "Frontier generals are often lawless—you may punish them severely."

sentences.zh: 原州守將武悍自用，以鑒年少易之，鑒發其奸，守將坐免，郡縣聞風無敢犯者。

translations.literal: The garrison commander of Yuanzhou was fierce, brutal, and self-willed; he took Jian's youth lightly. Jian exposed his wrongdoing; the commander was dismissed from office, and throughout the prefectures and counties none dared to offend upon hearing of this.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander of Yuanzhou was brutal and headstrong and underestimated Jian because he was young. Jian exposed his crimes; the commander was dismissed, and throughout the circuit none dared to transgress once they heard of it.

sentences.zh: 齊廢，除知城陽軍，改山東東路轉運副使，攝行台左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished he was appointed military commander of Chengyang Army, transferred to deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong East circuit, and acted as director of the left bureau on the mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished he was made commander of Chengyang Army, deputy transport commissioner of the Shandong East circuit, and acting director of the left bureau on the mobile secretariat.

sentences.zh: 行台宰相欲以故宋宦者權都水監，鑒曰：「誤國閹豎，汴人視為寇仇，付以美官，將失人望。」

translations.literal: The chancellor of the mobile secretariat wished to appoint a former Song eunuch to act as director of waterways. Jian said: "The castrated minions who ruined the state—the people of Bian regard them as hated enemies. To give them a fine office will lose the people's regard."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of the mobile secretariat wanted to put a former Song eunuch in charge of waterways. Jian said, "Those castrated creatures who ruined the state—the people of Bian hate them as enemies. Giving them a fine office will cost you the people's respect."

sentences.zh: 遂不用。

translations.literal: The appointment was therefore not made.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was not made.

sentences.zh: 以母憂解職，天德初，起為濟州刺史，移涿州。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning; at the beginning of Tiande he was recalled as prefect of Jizhou and transferred to Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; at the beginning of Tiande he was recalled as prefect of Jizhou and transferred to Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 海陵召鑒入朝，應對失旨，遣還郡，俄除知火山軍，以病免。

translations.literal: Emperor Hailing summoned Jian to court; his responses missed the emperor's intent and he was sent back to his prefecture. Soon he was appointed commander of Huoshan Army but was excused on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hailing summoned Jian to court; his answers displeased the emperor and he was sent back to his post. He was soon made commander of Huoshan Army but resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 大定初，起知甯海軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was recalled as commander of Ninghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he was recalled as commander of Ninghai Army.

sentences.zh: 秋禾方熟，子方蟲生，鑒出城行視，蟲乃自死。

translations.literal: The autumn grain was just ripening when the Zifang insect appeared; Jian went out of the city to inspect, and the insects then died of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn grain was ripening when Zifang insects appeared; Jian went out to inspect the fields, and the pests died off on their own.

sentences.zh: 再遷鎮西軍節度使，改河北西路轉運使，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to military commissioner of the Zhenxi Army, transferred to transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to commissioner of the Zhenxi circuit, then transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 蒲察鄭留

translations.literal: Pucha Zhengliu
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhengliu

sentences.zh: 蒲察鄭留，字文叔，東京路斡底必剌猛安人。

translations.literal: Pucha Zhengliu, courtesy name Wenshu, was from the Gedibila battalion of the Eastern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Zhengliu, styled Wenshu, came from the Gedibila battalion of the Eastern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年進士，調高苑主薄、浚州司候，補尚書省令史，除鑒察御史，累遷北京、臨潢按察副使、戶部侍郎。
