translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the twenty-second year of Dading, was assigned as registrar of Gaoyuan and courier station officer of Junzhou, appointed clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, made investigating censor, and was eventually promoted to deputy inspector of the Northern Capital and Linhuang circuits and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-second year of Dading, served as registrar of Gaoyuan and courier officer of Junzhou, became a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, investigating censor, and eventually deputy inspector of the Northern Capital and Linhuang circuits and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏鄭留前任北京稱職，遷陝西路按察使，改順義軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Censorate reported that Zhengliu had performed his duties well in his previous post at the Northern Capital; he was transferred to inspector of the Shaanxi circuit and changed to military commissioner of the Shunyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported that Zhengliu had served well at the Northern Capital; he was made inspector of the Shaanxi circuit and then commissioner of the Shunyi circuit.

sentences.zh: 西京人李安兄弟爭財，府縣不能決，按察司移鄭留平理。

translations.literal: The brothers Li An of the Western Capital disputed over property; the prefecture and county could not decide the case, and the inspection office referred it to Zhengliu for settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Li An of the Western Capital were disputing an inheritance; the local authorities could not settle it, and the inspection office referred the case to Zhengliu.

sentences.zh: 月餘不問，會釋奠孔子廟，鄭留乃引安兄弟與諸生敘齒，列坐會酒，陳說古之友悌數事。

translations.literal: For more than a month he did not inquire into the case. When the sacrifice was offered at the Confucius temple, Zhengliu brought the Li brothers together with the students, arranged them by age, seated them for a banquet, and recounted several ancient stories of friendship and brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a month he took no formal action. At the Confucius temple sacrifice he brought the Li brothers together with the students, seated them by seniority for a banquet, and told several ancient stories of friendship and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 安兄弟感悟，謝曰：「節使父母也，誓不復爭。」

translations.literal: The Li brothers were moved to understanding and apologized, saying: "The commissioner is like a parent to us—we swear never to dispute again."
translations.idiomatic: The Li brothers were moved and apologized, saying, "You are like a parent to us—we swear never to quarrel again."

sentences.zh: 乃相讓而歸。

translations.literal: They then yielded to one another and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded to each other and went home.

sentences.zh: 朔州多盜，鄭留禁絕遊食，多蓄兵器，因行春撫諭之，盜乃衰息，獄空。

translations.literal: Shuozhou had many bandits; Zhengliu forbade vagrancy and the hoarding of weapons, and during the spring tour to comfort and instruct the people, banditry then declined and the prisons stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Shuozhou was rife with bandits; Zhengliu banned vagrancy and the hoarding of weapons, and on his spring tour to comfort the people banditry declined and the prisons emptied.

sentences.zh: 賜錫宴錢以褒之。

translations.literal: He was granted banquet money as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with banquet funds.

sentences.zh: 改利涉軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of the Lishe Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Lishe circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔括馬，鄭留使百姓飼養以須，御史劾之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the requisition of horses; Zhengliu had the people raise and feed them in readiness. The censors impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered horses requisitioned, Zhengliu had the people raise and feed them in readiness. The censors impeached him.

sentences.zh: 既而伐宋，諸語括馬皆瘦，惟隆州馬肥，乃釋鄭留。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when the campaign against Song was launched, the horses requisitioned in all circuits were lean, but only those of Longzhou were fat; Zhengliu was then released.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Song began, requisitioned horses from every circuit were thin—only those from Longzhou were fat—and Zhengliu was cleared.

sentences.zh: 大安初，徙安國軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, he was transferred to the Anguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Da'an era, he was transferred to Anguo.

sentences.zh: 二年，知慶陽府事。

translations.literal: In the second year, he became prefect of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the era, he was appointed prefect of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，夏人犯邊，鄭留擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Tangut raided the frontier; Zhengliu struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Xi Xia forces raided the border, and Zhengliu repelled them.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，改知平涼府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhi'ning, he was changed to prefect of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhi'ning, he was reassigned as prefect of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 是時，平涼新被兵，夏人複來攻，鄭留招潰卒為禦守計，夏兵退，遷官四階。

translations.literal: At that time Pingliang had recently suffered warfare; the Tangut again came to attack. Zhengliu gathered routed soldiers to plan defense; the Tangut army withdrew, and he was promoted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang had just been ravaged by war when the Tangut attacked again. Zhengliu rallied scattered troops to organize a defense; after the Tangut withdrew, he was promoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，改東京留守，致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, he was changed to governor of the Eastern Capital and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, he was made governor of the Eastern Capital and then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenyou.

sentences.zh: 鄭留重厚寡言笑，人不見其喜慍，臨終取奏稿盡焚之。

translations.literal: Zhengliu was grave and substantial, sparing of speech and laughter; people never saw him show joy or anger. At the end of his life he took his memorial drafts and burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengliu was sober and reserved, rarely speaking or laughing; no one ever saw him show pleasure or anger. On his deathbed he gathered his memorial drafts and burned them all.

sentences.zh: 女奚烈守愚

translations.literal: Nuxilie Shouyu
translations.idiomatic: Nuxilie Shouyu

sentences.zh: 女奚烈守愚，字仲晦，本名胡裏改門，真定府路吾直克猛安人也。

translations.literal: Nuxilie Shouyu, courtesy name Zhonghui, original name Huligaimen, was from the Wuzhike battalion of the Zhending circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Nuxilie Shouyu, styled Zhonghui, born Huligaimen, came from the Wuzhike battalion of the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 六歲知讀書。

translations.literal: At six he knew how to read.
translations.idiomatic: At age six he could read.

sentences.zh: 既齔，或謂食肉昏神識，乃戒而不食。

translations.literal: After his milk teeth fell, someone said that eating meat dulls one's spirit and consciousness, so he abstained and did not eat it.
translations.idiomatic: Once his baby teeth had fallen out, someone told him that meat clouded the mind, so he vowed to abstain and never ate it.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父沒時年十五，營葬如禮，治家有法，鄉人稱之。

translations.literal: His nature was deeply filial; when his father died he was fifteen, and he arranged the burial according to ritual. He governed the household by rule, and fellow villagers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he was fifteen when his father died; he conducted the funeral according to rite and ran the household with discipline, winning praise from his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 中明昌二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Mingchang.

sentences.zh: 調深澤主簿，治有聲。

translations.literal: He was assigned as registrar of Shenze, and his administration gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed registrar of Shenze, he quickly earned a reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 遷懷仁令，改弘文校理，秩滿為臨沂令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Huairen, changed to collator of the Hongwen Institute, and at the end of his term became magistrate of Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to magistrate of Huairen, then became a collator of the Hongwen Institute; when his term ended he was appointed magistrate of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 有不逞輩五百人，結為黨社，大擾境內，守愚下車，其黨散去。

translations.literal: There were five hundred unruly men who formed clubs and societies and greatly disturbed the district. When Shouyu arrived to take office, their cliques dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred unruly men had formed gangs that terrorized the county. The moment Shouyu took office, they disbanded and fled.

sentences.zh: 蝗起莒、密間，獨不入臨沂境。

translations.literal: Locusts arose between Ju and Mi, but alone did not enter Linyi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Locust swarms struck between Ju and Mi, but none entered Linyi.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷括河朔、山東地，隱匿者沒入宮。

translations.literal: Previously, the court had registered land in Hebei and Shandong; those who concealed holdings had them confiscated by the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had conducted a land survey in Hebei and Shandong; concealed property was confiscated for the crown.

sentences.zh: 告者給賞。

translations.literal: Informants were given rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Informants were paid bounties.

sentences.zh: 莒州刺史教其奴告臨沂人冒地，積賞錢三百萬，先給官鏹乃征於民，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Ju instructed his slave to denounce people of Linyi for falsely claiming land; the accumulated reward money reached three million cash. Official funds were paid out first and then levied on the people, who suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Ju had his slave denounce Linyi residents for falsely registering land, amassing three million cash in bounties. The prefecture paid the rewards from public funds first, then taxed the people to recover the cost, causing great hardship.

sentences.zh: 守愚列其冤狀白州，州不為理，即聞於戶部而征還之，流民歸業，縣人勒其事于石。

translations.literal: Shouyu set forth their grievances and reported to the prefecture; the prefecture would not act, so he notified the Ministry of Revenue, which ordered the levies returned. Migrants returned to their occupations, and the county people had the affair carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu laid out the injustice to the prefecture, which ignored it, so he reported to the Ministry of Revenue and had the levies refunded. Displaced people returned to their work, and the county had the story inscribed on stone.

sentences.zh: 改秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母喪，勺飲不入口三日，終喪未嘗至內寢。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took not a spoonful of drink for three days, and throughout the mourning period he never entered the inner chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took not a spoonful of drink for three days, and throughout mourning he never entered the inner chamber.

sentences.zh: 太常寺、勸農司交辟守愚，皆不聽，服除，除同知登聞檢院，改著作郎、永定軍節度副使。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Office for Encouraging Agriculture repeatedly invited Shouyu, but he would not accept; when mourning ended he was appointed deputy director of the Petition Review Office and changed to drafting secretary and deputy military commissioner of the Yongding Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Office for Encouraging Agriculture repeatedly invited Shouyu, but he refused; when mourning ended he was made deputy director of the Petition Review Office, then drafting secretary and deputy commissioner of the Yongding circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰和伐宋，守愚為山東行六部員外郎，改大興都總管判官。

translations.literal: During the Taihe campaign against Song, Shouyu served as vice director of the Six Ministries on the Shandong mobile staff and was changed to judicial administrator of the Daxing metropolitan command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe campaign against Song, Shouyu served as vice director of the Six Ministries on the Shandong mobile staff and became judicial administrator of the Daxing metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，除修起居注，轉刑部員外郎、戶部郎中、太子左諭德。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an he was appointed compiler of the Diarist Office, transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, director of the Ministry of Revenue, and left tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an he was appointed compiler of the Diarist Office, then vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, director of the Ministry of Revenue, and left tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，除戶部侍郎，數月拜諫議大夫、提點近侍局。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was appointed vice minister of revenue; within months he was made remonstrance grandee and director of the Inner Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he was made vice minister of revenue; within months he was appointed remonstrance grandee and director of the Inner Service Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二年，除保大軍節度使，改翰林學士、參議陝西路安撫司事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoda Army and changed to Hanlin academician and adviser on the Shaanxi West Route Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made military commissioner of the Baoda circuit and Hanlin academician advising the Shaanxi West Route Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 安撫完顏弼重其為人，每事咨而後行。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Bi valued his character and consulted him on every matter before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Bi valued his character and consulted him before acting on every matter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有疾，詔賜禦藥。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill, and an edict bestowed imperial medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill, and the throne sent imperial medicine.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died.

sentences.zh: 守愚為人忠實無華，孜孜于公，蓋天性然也。

translations.literal: Shouyu as a man was loyal and sincere without ornament, tireless in public service—it was simply his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu was plainspoken, loyal, and tireless in public duty—simply the man he was by nature.

sentences.zh: 石抹元

translations.literal: Shi Moyuan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Moyuan

sentences.zh: 石抹元，字希明，懿州路胡土虎猛安人。

translations.literal: Shi Moyuan, courtesy name Ximing, was from the Hutu battalion of the Yizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Moyuan, styled Ximing, came from the Hutu battalion of the Yizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪父，號泣不食者數日。

translations.literal: At seven he lost his father and wailed without eating for several days.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven his father died; he wept and refused food for days.

sentences.zh: 十三居母喪如成人。

translations.literal: At thirteen he observed mourning for his mother like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he observed his mother's mourning rites as a grown man would.

sentences.zh: 嘗為擊鞠戲，馬踣，歎曰：「生無兄弟，而數乘此險，設有不測，奈何？」

translations.literal: Once when playing cuju, his horse stumbled, and he sighed: "Born without brothers, yet I repeatedly take such risks—if something unforeseen should happen, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Once while playing cuju his horse fell, and he sighed: "I have no brothers, yet I keep taking such risks—if something went wrong, what would become of my family?"

sentences.zh: 由是終身不復為之。

translations.literal: From then on he never played it again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He never played again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 補樞密院尚書省譯史，調同知恩州軍州事，遷監察御史，為同知淄州軍州事。

translations.literal: He was appointed interpreter-clerk of the Council of State and Ministry of Revenue, assigned as vice prefect of Enzhou, promoted to investigating censor, and made vice prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an interpreter-clerk in the Council of State and Ministry of Revenue, then as vice prefect of Enzhou, investigating censor, and vice prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 劇盜劉奇久為民患，一日捕獲，方訊鞫，聞赦將至，亟命杖殺之，闔郡稱快。

translations.literal: The notorious bandit Liu Qi had long plagued the people; one day he was captured, and while he was being interrogated, word came that an amnesty was imminent. Yuan urgently ordered him beaten to death, and the whole prefecture rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The notorious bandit Liu Qi had long terrorized the people. When he was captured and under interrogation, word came that an amnesty was near. Yuan immediately had him beaten to death, to the relief of the entire prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改大興府判官，沂王府司馬、沁南軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to judge of Daxing Prefecture, master of ceremonies of the Yi Prince's household, and deputy military commissioner of the Qinnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became judge of Daxing Prefecture, master of ceremonies of the Yi Prince's household, and deputy commissioner of the Qinnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 河內民家有多美橙者，歲獲厚利。

translations.literal: A household in Henei had many fine oranges and each year gained rich profit.
translations.idiomatic: A family in Henei owned many fine orange trees and reaped handsome profits each year.

sentences.zh: 仇家夜入殘毀之，主人捕得，乃以劫財誣其人，仇家引服，贓不可得。

translations.literal: A rival family entered by night and destroyed them. The owner captured the man and then falsely accused him of robbery; the rival confessed, but no stolen goods could be found.
translations.idiomatic: A rival family broke in at night and destroyed the trees. The owner captured one of them and then falsely accused him of robbery. The rival confessed, but no loot could be found.

sentences.zh: 元攝州事，究得其情。

translations.literal: Yuan was acting prefect and investigated until he got the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was acting prefect; he investigated and uncovered the truth.

sentences.zh: 尋改河北西路轉運副使，累遷山東西路按察轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to deputy transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit and was eventually promoted to inspection and transport commissioner of the Shandong West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became deputy transport commissioner of western Hebei and eventually inspector and transport commissioner of western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，黃摑吾典徵兵東平，擁眾不進，大括民財，眾皆忿怨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, Huang Jiadian was requisitioning troops at Dongping; he held his force but would not advance and greatly extorted the people's wealth, and all were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou, Huang Jiadian was conscripting troops at Dongping. He held a large force but refused to advance, extorting the people's wealth and arousing widespread anger.

sentences.zh: 副統僕散掃合殺吾典於坐，取其符佩之，縱恣尤甚。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Puxian Saoge killed Jiadian at his seat, took his tally and wore it, and behaved with even greater license.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Puxian Saoge killed Jiadian at table, seized his credentials, and behaved with even greater impunity.

sentences.zh: 元密疏劾掃合擅殺近臣，無上不道，掃合坐誅。

translations.literal: Yuan sent a secret memorial impeaching Saoge for executing a near minister on his own authority—a capital offense against the ruler. Saoge was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan submitted a secret memorial accusing Saoge of unlawfully killing a court official—a capital offense. Saoge was executed.

sentences.zh: 移知濟南府，到官六月卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to know the affairs of Jinan Prefecture; six months after taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jinan and died six months after taking office.

sentences.zh: 元生平寡言笑，尚節儉，居官自守，不交權要，人以是稱之。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Yuan was sparing of speech and laughter, valued frugality, kept himself upright in office, and did not associate with the powerful, and for this people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was reticent and frugal by nature, kept his own counsel in office, and avoided the powerful—qualities for which people respected him.

sentences.zh: 張彀，字伯英，許州臨潁人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gou, courtesy name Boying, was a native of Yingchuan in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gou, styled Boying, came from Yingchuan in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士，調甯陵縣主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading and was assigned as registrar of Ningling County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading and was assigned registrar of Ningling County.

sentences.zh: 改泰定軍節度判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to judicial administrator of the Taiding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became judicial administrator of the Taiding circuit.

sentences.zh: 率儒士行鄉飲酒禮。

translations.literal: He led the scholar-gentry in performing the district drinking ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He led local scholars in performing the district drinking ceremony.

sentences.zh: 改同州觀察判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to observation judicial administrator of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became observation judicial administrator of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是時，出兵備邊，州征箭十萬，限以雕雁羽為之，其價翔躍不可得。

translations.literal: At that time troops were sent to guard the frontier; the prefecture was levied one hundred thousand arrows, restricted to being made from eagle and wild-goose feathers, whose price soared and could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were sent to guard the frontier; the prefecture was ordered to supply one hundred thousand arrows, which had to be fletched with eagle and wild-goose feathers—feathers whose price had soared beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 彀曰：「矢去物也，何羽不可。」

translations.literal: Gou said: "An arrow is a disposable thing—what feather may not be used?"
translations.idiomatic: Gou said, "An arrow is expendable—what feather cannot serve?"

sentences.zh: 節度使曰：「當須省報。」

translations.literal: The military commissioner said: "This must be reported to the province."
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioner said, "That must be reported to the province."

sentences.zh: 彀曰：「州距京師二千里，如民急何。

translations.literal: Gou said: "The prefecture is two thousand li from the capital—what of the people's urgency?
translations.idiomatic: Gou said, "The prefecture is two thousand li from the capital—what of the people's urgent need?

sentences.zh: 萬一有責，下官身任其咎。」

translations.literal: If blame should come, this subordinate official will bear the fault himself."
translations.idiomatic: If there is blame, I will bear it myself."

sentences.zh: 一日之間，價減數倍。

translations.literal: Within a single day the price fell several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day the price fell severalfold.

sentences.zh: 尚書省竟如所請。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue in the end approved as he had requested.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue ultimately approved his request.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史，除同知鄭州防禦使事，改北京鹽使。

translations.literal: He was appointed a clerk of the Ministry of Revenue, made deputy defender of Zhengzhou, and changed to salt commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Ministry of Revenue clerk, made deputy defender of Zhengzhou, and then salt commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，再遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when mourning ended he was again promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was promoted again to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 從伐宋，遷武寧軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Song, he was transferred to deputy military commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Song he was made deputy military commissioner of the Wuning circuit.

sentences.zh: 居母憂。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，改惠民司令，曆河南治中、顯州刺史、刑部郎中、同知河南府事，遷河東南路轉運使、權行六部尚書，安撫使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was changed to director of the Office for People's Benefit, successively served as administrative aide of Henan, prefect of Xianzhou, director of the Ministry of Punishments, and deputy prefect of Henan Prefecture, and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong South Route, acting director of the Six Ministries, and pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he became director of the Office for People's Benefit, then served as Henan administrative aide, prefect of Xianzhou, director of the Ministry of Punishments, and deputy prefect of Henan Prefecture, and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong South Route, acting director of the Six Ministries, and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 彀天性孝友，任子悉先諸弟，俸入所得亦委其弟掌之，未嘗問有無雲。

translations.literal: Gou was filial and fraternal by nature; whenever conferring official appointments he always put his younger brothers ahead, and salary income he also entrusted to his younger brothers to manage, never even asking whether they had enough.
translations.idiomatic: By nature filial and devoted to his brothers, Gou always placed his younger brothers ahead when handing out official appointments, entrusted all his salary to them to manage, and never even asked whether they had enough.

sentences.zh: 趙重福

translations.literal: Zhao Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 趙重福，字履祥，豐州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhongfu, courtesy name Lüxiang, was a man of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhongfu, styled Lüxiang, was from Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 通女直大小字，試補女直誥院令史。

translations.literal: He mastered large and small Jurchen script and on trial appointment was made clerk of the Jurchen Edict Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in Jurchen large and small script, he entered service as a clerk in the Jurchen Edict Office.

sentences.zh: 轉兵部譯史、陝西提刑知法，遷陝西東路都勾判官、右藏庫副使、同知陳州防禦事。

translations.literal: He transferred to interpreter-clerk of the Ministry of War, judicial knowing-the-law of Shaanxi, and was promoted to chief registrar of the Shaanxi East circuit, deputy keeper of the Right Treasury, and vice commissioner of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became a war ministry interpreter, Shaanxi judicial officer, then chief registrar of eastern Shaanxi, deputy keeper of the Right Treasury, and vice commissioner of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋諜人蘇泉入河南，重福跡之，至魚台將渡河，見前一舟且渡，令從者大呼泉姓名，前舟中忽有蒼惶失措者，執之果泉也。

translations.literal: The Song spy Su Quan entered Henan; Zhongfu tracked him. At Yutai, about to cross the river, he saw a boat ahead about to ferry across and ordered his followers to shout Quan's name. In the boat ahead someone suddenly panicked; they seized him, and it was indeed Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song spy Su Quan entered Henan, Zhongfu tracked him down. At Yutai, as a boat ahead was about to cross the river, he had his men shout Quan's name. Someone aboard panicked; they seized him, and it was Quan.

sentences.zh: 改滄州鹽副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant salt commissioner of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant salt commissioner of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，民煮鹵為鹽賣以給食，鹽官往往杖殺之。

translations.literal: In a year of famine the people boiled brine to make salt and sold it for food; salt officials often had them beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year, people boiled brine into salt to sell for food, and salt officials often had them beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 重福曰：「寧使課殿，不忍殺人。」

translations.literal: Zhongfu said: "I would rather fall short of the revenue quota than slaughter people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu said, "I would rather miss the revenue target than kill people."

sentences.zh: 歲滿，課殿當降，尚書右丞完顏匡、三司使按出虎知其事，乃以歲荒薄其罰，除織染署令。

translations.literal: When his term ended, failing the quota he should have been demoted, but Right Vice Minister Wanyan Kuang and Fiscal Commissioner An Chuhu knew the circumstances and, on account of the year's famine, reduced the penalty; he was appointed director of the Weaving and Dyeing Office.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he should have been demoted for missing the quota, but Vice Minister Wanyan Kuang and Fiscal Commissioner An Chuhu knew what he had done and, given the famine, mitigated the penalty. He was appointed director of the Weaving and Dyeing Office.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，佐戶部尚書張煒調兵食于古北口，遷都水少監，行西北路六部郎中，治密雲縣，俄兼戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he assisted Minister of Revenue Zhang Wei in arranging troops and provisions at Gubeikou, was promoted to vice director of waterways, acting director of the Six Ministries of the Northwest circuit, governed Miyun County, and soon concurrently served as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an he helped Revenue Minister Zhang Wei supply troops at Gubeikou, became vice director of waterways and acting head of the northwest Six Ministries while governing Miyun County, and soon added a concurrent post as vice director of revenue.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，以守密雲功遷同知河間府事，行六部侍郎，權清州防禦使，攝河北東路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, for merit in defending Miyun he was promoted to vice prefect of Hejian, acting vice minister of the Six Ministries, provisional commissioner of Qingzhou, and acting overall commander of military and horses of the Hebei East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, for defending Miyun he was made vice prefect of Hejian, acting vice minister of the Six Ministries, provisional commissioner of Qingzhou, and acting commander of eastern Hebei forces.

sentences.zh: 三年，河間被圍，有劉中者嘗與重福密雲聯事，勸重福出降，重福不聽。

translations.literal: In the third year Hejian was besieged; a certain Liu Zhong, who had once worked with Zhongfu at Miyun, urged Zhongfu to surrender; Zhongfu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Hejian was besieged, Liu Zhong, who had served with Zhongfu at Miyun, urged him to surrender. Zhongfu refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，河間兵少，多羸疾不任戰，欲亡去。

translations.literal: At that time Hejian had few troops; many were weak or ill and unfit for battle and wanted to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian had too few troops; many were sick or weak and unfit to fight, and wanted to desert.

sentences.zh: 重福勸其父老率其子弟，強者戰、弱者守，會久雨圍乃解去。

translations.literal: Zhongfu urged the elders to lead their sons and younger men—the strong to fight and the weak to defend—and by chance prolonged rain fell and the siege then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu persuaded the elders to rally their sons: the strong would fight, the weak would defend. After days of heavy rain the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 遷河東北路轉運使，致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong North circuit and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was made transport commissioner of northern Hedong and retired.

sentences.zh: 元光二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanguang, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yuanguang.

sentences.zh: 武都，字文伯、東勝州人。

translations.literal: Wu Dou, courtesy name Wenbo, was a man of Dongsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dou, styled Wenbo, was from Dongsheng.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年進士，調陽穀主簿，遷商水令。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the twenty-second year of Dading, was assigned as registrar of Yanggu, and was promoted to magistrate of Shangshui.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twenty-second year of Dading, he served as registrar of Yanggu and then magistrate of Shangshui.

sentences.zh: 縣素多盜，凡奸民嘗縱火行劫、椎埋發塚者，都皆廉得姓名，榜之通衢，約毋再犯，悉奔他境。

translations.literal: The county had long had many bandits; of all wicked men who had set fires to rob, buried victims secretly, or robbed graves, Dou had thoroughly learned their names, posted them at the crossroads, and pledged that they must not offend again—all fled to other regions.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long been plagued by bandits. Dou identified every arsonist, robber, grave robber, and corpse-burier by name, posted the list at the crossroads, and warned them never to offend again. They all fled the county.

sentences.zh: 察廉，遷南京路轉運支度判官，累遷中都路都轉運副使。

translations.literal: Recognized for incorruptibility, he was promoted to judge of fiscal supply of the Nanjing circuit and eventually to deputy overall transport commissioner of the Central Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Marked for integrity, he became judge of fiscal supply for the Nanjing circuit and eventually deputy transport commissioner of the Central Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 以親老，與弟監察御史鬱俱乞侍。

translations.literal: Because his parents were aged, he and his younger brother Yu, an investigating censor, both requested leave to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents grew old, he and his brother Yu, an investigating censor, both asked leave to care for them.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，調太原治中，複為都轉運副使，遷灤州刺史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was assigned as administrative aide of Taiyuan, again became deputy overall transport commissioner, and was promoted to prefect of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as aide to the Taiyuan prefect, again as deputy transport commissioner, and then as prefect of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 充宣差北京路規措官，都拘括散逸官錢百萬。

translations.literal: He served as imperial commissioner organizing affairs of the Northern Capital circuit; Dou requisitioned a million cash of scattered and lost official funds.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial commissioner for the Northern Capital circuit he recovered a million cash in lost official funds.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部郎中，權右司郎中，奏事稱旨。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Revenue, acting director of the Right Office, and in presenting affairs pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he served as a revenue director and acting right-office director; his memorials pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 被詔由海道漕遼東粟賑山東，都高其價直募人入粟，招海賈船致之。

translations.literal: By edict he was to ship grain from Liaodong by sea route to relieve Shandong; Dou raised the price to recruit people to contribute grain and summoned merchant ships to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to ship Liaodong grain by sea to relieve Shandong, he offered high prices to recruit grain and chartered merchant ships to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 三遷中都、西京按察副使。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became deputy inspector of the Central Capital and Western Capital circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became deputy inspector of the Central and Western Capital circuits.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，充宣差行六部侍郎，以勞遷本路按察使，行西南路六部尚書，佐元帥抹撚盡忠備禦西京，有勞，召為戶部尚書，賞銀二百兩、絹一百匹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he served as imperial commissioner and acting vice minister of the Six Ministries; for his labors he was promoted to inspector of his circuit, acting minister of the Six Ministries of the Southwest circuit, and assisted Marshal Moquan Jinzhong in defending the Western Capital. For his merit he was summoned as minister of revenue and rewarded with two hundred taels of silver and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an he served as imperial commissioner and acting vice minister of the Six Ministries. For his service he became circuit inspector and acting minister of the Southwest Six Ministries, assisting Marshal Moquan Jinzhong in the defense of the Western Capital. For this he was recalled as minister of revenue and awarded two hundred taels of silver and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，議衛紹王降封，語在《衛紹王紀》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, the court debated demoting Prince Shao of Wei; the account is in the Annals of Prince Shao of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, the court debated demoting Prince Shao of Wei—the account appears in his annals.

sentences.zh: 頃之，中都戒嚴，都知大興府，佩虎符便宜行事，彈壓中外軍民。

translations.literal: Before long the Central Capital was under martial law; Dou governed Daxing Prefecture, wore the tiger tally to act on discretionary authority, and suppressed both internal and external military and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Soon martial law was declared in the Central Capital. Dou became prefect of Daxing, with discretionary authority over military and civilians throughout the city.

sentences.zh: 都醉酒以褻衣見詔使，坐是解職。

translations.literal: Dou, drunk, received the imperial envoy in indecent dress; for this he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he received an imperial envoy in disheveled clothes and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 起為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was raised again as minister of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 中都解圍，為河東路宣撫使，俄以參知政事胥鼎代之。

translations.literal: When the siege of the Central Capital was lifted, he became pacification commissioner of the Hedong circuit; soon Vice Minister Xu Ding replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of the Central Capital was lifted, he became pacification commissioner of Hedong, but was soon replaced by Vice Minister Xu Ding.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the first year of Xingding.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈德

translations.literal: Geshilie De
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie De

sentences.zh: 紇石烈德，字廣之，真定路山春猛安人。

translations.literal: Geshilie De, courtesy name Guangzhi, was from the Shanchun battalion of the Zhending circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie De, styled Guangzhi, came from the Shanchun battalion of the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年進士，調南京教授。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Mingchang and was assigned as instructor of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the second year of Mingchang, he was appointed instructor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 察廉能，遷厭次令，補尚書省令史，除同知泗州防禦事、監察御史、大名治中、安、曹、裕三州刺史，曆同知臨潢，大興府事。

translations.literal: Recognized for incorruptibility and ability, he was promoted to magistrate of Yanci, appointed clerk of the Ministry of Revenue, made vice commissioner of Sizhou, investigating censor, administrative aide of Daming, prefect of An, Cao, and Yu prefectures, and successively served as vice governor of Linhuang and governor of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Marked for integrity and talent, he rose to magistrate of Yanci, became a revenue clerk, then vice commissioner of Sizhou, investigating censor, Daming aide, and prefect of An, Cao, and Yu, and eventually vice governor of Linhuang and governor of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷肇州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was promoted to commissioner of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he became commissioner of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，肇州升為武興軍節度，德為節度使宣撫司署都提控。

translations.literal: That year Zhaozhou was elevated to the Wuxing Army circuit; De served as overall controller of the military commissioner's pacification office.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhaozhou was elevated to the Wuxing circuit, and De became overall controller of the pacification headquarters.

sentences.zh: 肇州圍急，食且盡，有糧三百船在鴨子河，去州五裏不能至。

translations.literal: The siege of Zhaozhou was urgent and food was nearly exhausted; three hundred grain boats were on the Yazi River five li from the prefecture but could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhou was under heavy siege and nearly out of food. Three hundred grain boats sat on the Yazi River five li away but could not reach the city.

sentences.zh: 德乃浚濠增陴，築甬道導濠水屬之河。

translations.literal: De then dredged the moat and raised the ramparts, built a causeway, and channeled moat water to connect with the river.
translations.idiomatic: De dredged the moat, raised the walls, built a causeway, and linked the moat to the river.

sentences.zh: 鑿陷馬阱，伏甲其傍以拒守，一日兵數接，士殊死戰。

translations.literal: He dug horse traps, hid armored troops beside them to hold the defense; in one day the armies clashed repeatedly and the soldiers fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He dug horse traps, posted armored troops beside them, and fought off repeated assaults in a day of desperate battle.

sentences.zh: 渠成，船至城下，兵食足，圍乃解。

translations.literal: When the channel was complete the boats reached below the wall, troops had sufficient food, and the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When the channel was finished the boats reached the walls, supplies were restored, and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 改遼東路轉運使，軍民遮道挽留，乘夜乃得去。

translations.literal: He was changed to transport commissioner of the Liaodong circuit; soldiers and civilians blocked the road to detain him, and only by traveling at night could he leave.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to transport commissioner of Liaodong, he had to leave by night because soldiers and civilians blocked the road to keep him.

sentences.zh: 蒲鮮萬奴逼上京，德與部將劉子元戰卻之。

translations.literal: Puxian Wannu pressed upon the Upper Capital; De and his subordinate general Liu Ziyuan fought and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Puxian Wannu besieged the Upper Capital, De and his lieutenant Liu Ziyuan fought him off.

sentences.zh: 遷東京留守，曆保靜、武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to governor of the Eastern Capital and successively served as military commissioner of the Baojing and Wusheng armies.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of the Eastern Capital and later commissioner of the Baojing and Wusheng circuits.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，以本官行六部事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding, with his existing rank he directed the affairs of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingding he served in his existing rank as acting head of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 三年，以節度權元帥右都監，與左都監單州經略使完顏仲元俱行元帥府于宿州。

translations.literal: In the third year, with his commissioner's rank he served as provisional right overseer of the marshal's office; together with Left Overseer Wanyan Zhongyuan, pacification commissioner of Danzhou, he ran the marshal's headquarters at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as acting right overseer of the marshalate, he and Left Overseer Wanyan Zhongyuan, pacification commissioner of Danzhou, jointly directed the marshal's headquarters at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 明年，召還中都。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned back to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year.

sentences.zh: 張特立

translations.literal: Zhang Teli
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Teli

sentences.zh: 張特立，字文舉，曹州東明人。

translations.literal: Zhang Teli, courtesy name Wenju, was a man of Dongming in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Teli, styled Wenju, was from Dongming in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年中進士第，調宣德州司候。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he passed the civil service examination and was assigned as courier officer of Xude Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taihe and was appointed courier officer of Xude Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 郡多皇族巨室，特立律之以法，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: The prefecture had many imperial clansmen and great houses; Teli restrained them by law, and the whole territory became solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was full of imperial clansmen and powerful families; Teli enforced the law impartially and the whole region fell into order.

sentences.zh: 調萊州節度判官，不赴，躬耕杞之圉城，以經學自樂。

translations.literal: He was assigned as judge of the Laizhou military commission but did not take up the post; he personally farmed at Yucheng in Qi and took joy in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned judge of the Laizhou circuit, he declined the post and instead farmed at Yucheng in Qi, finding joy in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 正大初，左丞侯摯、參政師安石薦其才，授洛陽令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda, Left Vice Minister Hou Zhi and Vice Minister Shi Anshi recommended his talent, and he was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengda, Left Vice Minister Hou Zhi and Vice Minister Shi Anshi recommended him, and he was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 拜章言：「鎬、厲二宅，久加禁錮，棘圍柝警，如防寇盜。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "The residences of Hao and Li have long been placed under strict confinement, with thorn hedges and watch-beats as if guarding against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "The households of Hao and Li have long been held under strict confinement, ringed with thorn hedges and night watches as though guarding against bandits.

sentences.zh: 近降赦恩。

translations.literal: Recently an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was recently proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 謀反大逆，皆蒙湔雪，彼獨何罪，幽囚若是。

translations.literal: Those guilty of plotting rebellion and great treason have all been cleansed and pardoned—what crime have they alone committed, that they are imprisoned in darkness like this?
translations.idiomatic: Plotters and traitors have all been pardoned—what crime have they alone committed, that they remain shut away in darkness like this?

sentences.zh: 世宗神靈在天，得無傷其心乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's spirit is in Heaven—can this fail to wound his heart!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong's spirit watches from Heaven—can this fail to wound his heart!

sentences.zh: 聖嗣未立，未必不由是也。」

translations.literal: The sacred heir has not been established—perhaps it is not unrelated to this."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial heir has not been established—perhaps this is not unrelated."

sentences.zh: 又言：「方今三面受敵，百姓凋敝，宰執非才，臣恐中興之功未可以歲月期也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "At present we face enemies on three sides; the people are exhausted and impoverished; the chief ministers lack ability—I fear the work of restoration cannot be expected within a few years."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The realm faces enemies on three sides; the people are exhausted; the chief ministers lack ability—I fear restoration cannot be achieved within a few years."

sentences.zh: 又言：「尚書右丞顏盞世魯遣其奴與小民爭田，失大臣體。

translations.literal: He also said: "Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue Yanzhan Shilu sent his slave to dispute fields with commoners—this falls short of a great minister's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Right Vice Minister Yanzhan Shilu sent his slave to dispute land with commoners—this is unworthy of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 參知政事徒單兀典諂事近習，得居其位。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of State Tushan Wudian fawned on those close to the throne and thereby obtained his post.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Tushan Wudian fawned on the emperor's intimates and thereby won his post.

sentences.zh: 皆宜罷之。」

translations.literal: All should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Both should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 當路者忌其直，陰有以擠之。

translations.literal: Those in power resented his forthrightness and secretly sought means to squeeze him out.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power resented his bluntness and secretly plotted to force him out.

sentences.zh: 因劾省掾高楨輩受請托，飲娼家。

translations.literal: He therefore impeached the provincial clerks Gao Zhen and others for accepting bribes and drinking at brothels.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore impeached provincial clerks including Gao Zhen for accepting bribes and drinking at brothels.

sentences.zh: 時平章政事白撒犒軍陝西歸，楨等泣訴於道，以當時同席並有省掾王賓，張為其進士，故不劾。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Councilor Bai Sa was returning from rewarding the troops in Shaanxi; Zhen and the others wept and appealed to him on the road. Because at the time Wang Bin, also a provincial clerk, had shared the same table—and Zhang was his jinshi fellow—he did not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Bai Sa was then returning from rewarding troops in Shaanxi; Zhen and the others wept and appealed to him on the road. Because provincial clerk Wang Bin had shared the same table—and Zhang was his jinshi fellow—he did not impeach Bin.

sentences.zh: 白撒以其私且不實，並治特立及賓。

translations.literal: Bai Sa, judging this partiality and lack of truth, punished both Teli and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Sa judged this partial and unfounded, and punished both Teli and Bin.

sentences.zh: 特立左遷邳州軍事判官，杖五十，賓亦勒停。

translations.literal: Teli was demoted to military judicial administrator of Pizhou and flogged fifty strokes; Bin was also suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: Teli was demoted to military judicial administrator of Pizhou and flogged fifty strokes; Bin was suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 士論皆惜特立之去。

translations.literal: Scholar-official opinion universally regretted Teli's departure.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere regretted Teli's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 後卒癸丑歲，年七十五。

translations.literal: He later died in the year guichou, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in the guichou year, at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 王浩，由吏起身，初辟涇陽令，廉白為關輔第一。

translations.literal: Wang Hao rose from clerical service; he was first recommended as magistrate of Jingyang, and his integrity was ranked first in the Guanfu region.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao rose from clerical service; he was first recommended as magistrate of Jingyang, and his integrity was ranked first in the Guanfu region.

sentences.zh: 時西台檄州縣增植棗果，督責嚴急，民甚被擾，浩獨無所問，主司將坐之，浩曰：「是縣所植已滿其數，若欲增植，必盜他人所有，取彼置此，未見其利。」

translations.literal: At that time the Western Secretariat ordered prefectures and counties to increase plantings of jujubes and fruit trees, with supervision strict and urgent; the people were greatly harassed. Hao alone made no inquiry. The supervising office was about to punish him, but Hao said: "This county's plantings already meet the quota; if more are required, one must steal what belongs to others—taking from there to place here, I see no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Western Secretariat ordered prefectures and counties to increase plantings of jujubes and fruit trees under harsh supervision; the people were greatly harassed. Hao alone made no demand. The supervising office was about to punish him, but Hao said, "This county's plantings already meet the quota; to plant more would mean seizing others' property—taking from there to place here, I see no benefit."

sentences.zh: 其愛民多此類。

translations.literal: His love for the people was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the people in many such ways.

sentences.zh: 所在有善政，民絲毫無所犯，秦人為立生祠，歲時思之。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he had good government; the people suffered not the slightest harm, and the people of Qin built him a living shrine and remembered him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served his governance was good; the people suffered no harm, and the people of Qin built him a living shrine and remembered him at the seasons.

sentences.zh: 南遷後，為扶溝令。

translations.literal: After the southward move he served as magistrate of Fugou.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south he served as magistrate of Fugou.

sentences.zh: 開興元年正月，民錢大亨等執縣官送款于北，大亨以浩有恩於民，不忍加刃，日遣所知勸之降，浩終不聽，於是殺之，無血。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Kaixing, the people Qian Daheng and others seized the county officials and offered surrender to the north. Daheng, because Hao had shown kindness to the people, could not bear to strike him with a blade; day after day he sent acquaintances to urge him to surrender, but Hao would not listen, and so they killed him—without blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Kaixing, Qian Daheng and others seized the county officials and offered surrender to the north. Because Hao had been kind to the people, Daheng could not bear to strike him; day after day he sent acquaintances to urge him to surrender, but Hao refused, and so they killed him—without blood.

sentences.zh: 主簿劉坦、尉宋乙並見害。

translations.literal: Registrar Liu Tan and sheriff Song Yi were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Liu Tan and sheriff Song Yi were also killed.

sentences.zh: 棄屍道路，自春徂夏，獨浩屍儼然如生，目且不瞑，烏犬莫敢近，殆若有神護者。

translations.literal: The corpses were abandoned on the road; from spring until summer, Hao's corpse alone remained upright as if alive, his eyes unclosed; crows and dogs did not dare approach—it was as if some spirit protected him.
translations.idiomatic: The corpses were abandoned on the road; from spring until summer, Hao's corpse alone remained upright as if alive, his eyes unclosed; crows and dogs dared not approach—as if a spirit protected him.

sentences.zh: 初，辟舉法行，縣官甚多得人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the recommendation system was in force, county officials were in many cases well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When the recommendation system was in force, county posts were often filled with capable men.

sentences.zh: 如咸甯令張天綱、長安令李獻甫、洛陽令張特立三人有傳。

translations.literal: Such as the magistrates of Xianning, Zhang Tiangang; Chang'an, Li Xianfu; and Luoyang, Zhang Teli—these three have biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates Zhang Tiangang of Xianning, Li Xianfu of Chang'an, and Zhang Teli of Luoyang have biographies here.

sentences.zh: 余如興平師夔、臨潼武天禎、氾水黨君玉、偃師王登庸、高陵宋九嘉、登封薛居中、長社李天翼、河津孫鼎臣、郟城李無党、滎陽李過庭、尉氏張瑜、長葛張子玉、猗氏安德璋、三原蕭邦傑、藍田張德直、葉縣劉從益皆清慎才敏，極一時之選，而能扶持百年將傾之祚者，亦曰吏得其人故也。

translations.literal: Others such as Shi Kui of Xingping, Wu Tianzhen of Lintong, Dang Junyu of Fanshui, Wang Dengyong of Yanshi, Song Jiujia of Gaoling, Xue Juzhong of Dengfeng, Li Tianyi of Changshe, Sun Dingchen of Hejin, Li Wudang of Jiaocheng, Li Guoting of Xingyang, Zhang Yu of Weishi, Zhang Ziyu of Changge, An Dezhang of Yishi, Xiao Bangjie of Sanyuan, Zhang Dezhi of Lantian, and Liu Congyi of Ye County were all pure, cautious, talented, and keen—the finest choices of their age. That the dynasty nearing collapse after a century could still be upheld is also said to be because officials obtained the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Others—Shi Kui of Xingping, Wu Tianzhen of Lintong, Dang Junyu of Fanshui, Wang Dengyong of Yanshi, Song Jiujia of Gaoling, Xue Juzhong of Dengfeng, Li Tianyi of Changshe, Sun Dingchen of Hejin, Li Wudang of Jiaocheng, Li Guoting of Xingyang, Zhang Yu of Weishi, Zhang Ziyu of Changge, An Dezhang of Yishi, Xiao Bangjie of Sanyuan, Zhang Dezhi of Lantian, and Liu Congyi of Ye County—were all upright, careful, and capable, the finest administrators of their day. That a dynasty a century old and near collapse could still be propped up was also because the right men held office.
